## October 27, 2026: PC save import (into 0.4.0)

Developed on `dev-0.5` (full record there, in TECHNICAL: "PC vs Xbox 360
saves", "IPA105 PC save import", "IPA105 crash ...", "IPA106 result ...")
and brought here on Stefan's approval once it worked.

`ios/src/save_convert.cpp` converts a PC v1.3 save (63,596 bytes, `20CM`) to
the Xbox 360 layout (62,688 bytes, `MC02`, version 0x10D): every 2- and
4-byte value byte-swapped field by field, Lua table flag bits reordered,
0xCD fillers to 0xAA, header CRC32s and MD5s recomputed. The map follows the
Xbox loader's read order (sub_822C3A60 -> sub_822C2998 -> sub_822C2D30):
gameplay section 0x34-0x4034, cash and settings, profile id, race count and
300 records (0x42AD), unlock bytes, 63x12 words, alias, 30 records at
0x5A51, FEPlayerCarDB (PC 0x5BC5 / Xbox 0x5BCD, 36,040 bytes), then a byte,
3032 bytes of career stats and the current car of 11 modes. Taken from a
career on the device (the template): the header prelude, the check word at
0x5A2D (the loader refuses a value that differs from the game's), the
options block (132 bytes on PC, 140 on the Xbox) and the end of the tail.
Field map source: sprintstate/nfs-mw-save-editor (GPL-3.0), the dbalatoni13
nfsmw decompilation (CC0), the generated code.

Failed attempts kept: IPA105 crashed on load (race count left
little-endian: the loader's signed clamp let a negative count overrun a
stack buffer); IPA106 loaded but crashed after My Cars (template car handles
left in the 11 current-car slots). IPA107 (dev-0.5): works, Stefan on the
iPad: My Cars shows the save's 89 cars, career, racing and saving work.
Logs: `/Users/bep1s/Developer/Debug/Most Wanted (2005) Debug/27 October 2026/nfsmw_ipa105_pc_save_crash_ipad.log`,
`nfsmw_ipa106_pc_save_missing_cars_crash_ipad.log`.

Import (`ios/src/save_manager.mm`): files starting `20CM` count as saves and
are converted with the first local career as template; none on the device
gives a message. Import failures now say why.

### IPA111: touch controls drawn into the native frame

Stefan approved (Oct 28). Branch `touch-overlay-native` (off `main`).
`touch_controls.mm`: with the native layer showing and not editing, the
touch view's `setNeedsDisplay`/`setNeedsDisplayInRect:` no longer touch its
layer; the changed rectangle is redrawn (same `drawRect:`, view opacity as a
transparency layer) into a kept BGRA bitmap at the screen scale, at most once
per run loop turn, and handed to `nfsmw_native_set_touch_overlay`. The layer
is emptied once. The mode follows the native layer (0.5 s check, and on each
redraw request); `[touch] drawn into the native frame / by UIKit` logged.
`native_renderer.mm`: one shared texture, updated only in the changed
rectangle, blended (premultiplied) over the whole drawable before the FPS
counter. Known limit: the texture is written while an earlier frame may read
it (at worst a knob half-moved for one frame). Cvar `ios_touch_native`,
default true (Extra Args `--ios_touch_native=false` restores the UIKit layer).

### IPA112: frame-step clock (experiment for D-005)

Stefan approved (Oct 28). Hypothesis: the main thread's clock reads jitter
~1 ms around the vblank they follow, so each frame's world/camera step is
slightly uneven at 60 fps while the screen gets an even 60. SDK hook
`tools/ios/patch_ios_frame_clock.py` (in prepare_sdk.py): a filter on
`Clock::QueryGuestTickCount` (all mftb/KeQueryPerformanceCounter reads).
`ios/src/frame_clock.cpp`: cvar `nfsmw_frame_clock_ms` (default 0 = off).
On the game's main thread only (first caller of the deferred-call hook
sub_823C8290), reads less than that many ms after the latest guest vblank
(the display refresh display_rate.mm publishes) return the vblank's time;
later reads stay real; never backwards. Logs `[frame-clock] on` and, every
300 vblanks, the main thread's reads by time after the vblank (<1, 1-2, 2-4,
4-8, 8-12, 12+ ms) and how many were snapped. Risks: a wait that polls the
clock right after a vblank waits up to the window longer; if the frame's
read sits near the window's edge, steps of 0/2 vblanks (worse). Also has
IPA111's touch fix.
Built `ios/build/NFSMW-0.4.1-frame-clock-112.ipa`, 30098542 bytes, SHA-256

IPA113 run with the switch (Oct 28 14:26-14:27, iPhone, 1x/60; log
`Debug/28 October 2026/nfsmw_ipa113_utf_fix.log`): `[frame-clock] on: main
thread 17f88d, reads up to 8 ms` (the UTF-16 file was read). The main-loop
thread reads the clock ~3 times per vblank, spread over the whole frame, and
the spread drifts: 8-12 ms after the vblank at first (774 of 906), later
4-8 ms (583 of 900); only 16-759 of ~900 reads per 300 vblanks snapped. So
the game's loop is not in step with the vblank: its phase drifts against the
display, and an 8 ms window snaps some frames' reads and not others. The
swaps (`between swaps` lines) run on another thread (t1570948) than the
main loop (1570957). Pacing 0-5 of 300 off. Inference: the snap as built
cannot give equal steps; a clock that advances one period per swap (on the
thread that swaps) would.

IPA114: frame clock v2 (`nfsmw_frame_clock_swap`, default false). On the
main loop thread and the thread that swaps (native renderer swap), the guest
clock advances by whole refresh periods at each swap (as many as really
passed, normally 1) and runs on the real clock in between, held at one tick
short of the next period; past two periods without a swap it runs again
(one period behind until the next swap). Never backwards per thread. Logs
`[frame-clock] v2 on` and every 300 swaps the periods per swap and how far
the virtual clock is behind the real one. Other threads untouched.

Screen recording (Stefan, Oct 28 14:37, iPhone, 1x/60, Motion blur and
Post-processing off, donuts; `Debug/28 October 2026/ScreenRecording_10-28-2026
14-37-39_1.MP4`, 37.4 s, 1320x2868, 2226 frames). Measured with an
AVFoundation script (per-frame mean luma difference on a 64x36 grid;
scratch tool, not in the repo). Recorder frame intervals: 2192 of 2225 at
16.6-16.7 ms. During motion a frame normally differs from the one before by
~4-6 (grey levels); 133 frames are near-identical (< 0.15) to the previous
one: an exact repeat of the picture. They come as stretches where every
other frame repeats (11.10-12.24 s: 26 repeats in 1.1 s; 15.57-16.30 s:
18), i.e. 30 fps motion shown at 60, plus scattered single repeats
(3.3-5.2 s, 6.3, 8.4, 25.7, 26.0 s). This is the judder, measured: the
screen gets 60 refreshes but only 30 distinct pictures in those stretches.
Whether the game swaps identical frames, or the renderer presents a frame
twice, needs the game log of the same run (none sent yet).
Game log of the recorded run (`nfsmw_ipa114_screen_recording_iphone.log`,
frame clock v2 on): the display went 48 -> 60 Hz at 14:37:39.67 (the
recording starting). Over 14:37:45-14:38:05, which covers the video's
repeat stretches (11-12 s, 15.6-16.3 s), every window is `pacing: 0 of 300
off`, 60.0 frames/s on screen and 300 of 300 swaps one period. So the game
swapped and the renderer presented 60 frames a second, each 16.7 ms apart,
yet every other picture was identical in those stretches. IPA92 (iPad) found
no frame repeating the previous one's vertex constants. Inference: the
picture repeats although the frame is new: the displayed texture (the
frame's last colour resolve, or a resolve kept from an earlier frame,
`1 resolves from earlier frames` in every gameplay line) is at times the
previous frame's picture. Next (proposed): a diagnostic that compares a row
of the displayed picture with the previous frame's and logs each repeat
with the final resolve's address and source.

is the previous frame's, draws drawn of total, resolves kept from earlier
frames; every 300 frames a count. Frame clock switches stay off by default.

Main loop found (Oct 28): sub_823B0008 polls mftb>>2, converts the time
since the last frame to seconds (scale at 0x82A2BEF8), waits until it is over
a constant (0x820624E8), clamps it (0x82062824), and runs the frame
sub_823AFE20 with r3 = fctiwz(elapsed * rate (0x82062DAC)), i.e. truncated,
then restarts its count from now (the remainder is lost). sub_823AFE20 turns
r3 back into a time step (r3 * 0x820AFE00 * 0x82062AD0) for the world
(sub_823C6500) and calls World_Service (sub_824CE048). Inference: frame
periods jitter around a whole number of ticks, so truncation sometimes gives
one tick less (remainder lost) and the frames around it more: the camera's
2x/0 steps.

IPA120: `tools/ios/patch_game_frame_ticks.py` (generated code, USA; also run
by generate_code.py): before that fctiwz, f9 goes through
`nfsmw_frame_ticks` (frame_clock.cpp). Cvar `nfsmw_frame_ticks` default 1:
the remainder is carried to the next frame (ticks add up to elapsed time);
0 = the game's truncation. Logs the constants once (`[frame-ticks] main
loop: rate ..., waits for over ..., clamps at ...`) and every 300 frames
elapsed x rate by band and the ticks run. Camera log and read-ahead stay on.

Threads (time profile, run 2): the game's main loop sub_823B0008 and its
frame sub_823AFE20 run on one guest thread (XThread9793); draws reach the
native renderer on the CP thread ("GPU Commands", NativeDraw/NativeSwap),
and RenderFrame on the render queue. Constants arrive as type-0 register
writes copied into the ring by the game (Oct 22 census: no LOAD_ALU_CONSTANT
traffic listed), so the CP cannot read a newer camera than the game wrote:
the step-ahead pattern is in what the game itself emitted.

Render hand-off found (Oct 28, from the trace's stacks): the main loop thread
(XThread9793, entry sub_8284FE40) spends its idle time in sub_823B0008 >
sub_823AFE20 > sub_823AFC68 > sub_82441050 > sub_82441DB0 > Sleep(0) (100 us
sleeps, KeDelayExecutionThread): waiting for the render state 0x82A2CF40 to
leave 1. sub_82441050 picks the frame's drawing path: if [0x82912F50+32] == 6
(and 0x82A2D1B4 == 0), flag 0x828FBB50 = 1 and sub_82441EF0 sets state 1 and
hands the frame to the render thread (Main XThread, entry sub_82593A58, busy
most of the time), and the main loop goes on to update the next frame while
it is drawn; otherwise sub_82441E70 (no hand-off). Hypothesis: the render
thread reads camera data that the main loop is already updating for the next
frame, so the drawn camera is one update ahead for 1-3 frames whenever the
two threads' timing lines up that way (varies with load, warm-up, cores).

IPA124: `nfsmw_frame_ticks` mode 2, default: in the existing hook before the
main loop's fctiwz, the frame's elapsed time f0 (ms) is replaced by one
display period (16.67 ms at 60 Hz), or more periods when real time has run
over 0.75 of a period ahead (frames missed on screen too); a debt beyond -2
or +4 periods resyncs (loading). The loop itself is not slowed. Rationale:
the screen shows one game frame per refresh (pacing 0 of 300 off), so the
world should advance one refresh per frame.

40 fps presentation fix (Stefan, Oct 28: before the final 0.4.2 tests):
native_renderer.mm paced presentation (caps below the display rate, e.g.
40 on 120 Hz) now keeps a fixed grid: each frame's target is the previous
target + one interval, moved on by whole intervals until it is at least the
recent GPU time (EMA of the frame GPU time, `recent_gpu_seconds`) + 4 ms
from now; restart from the last shown frame only when the previous target is
more than 4 intervals away. Before, the grid restarted from the last frame
actually shown each time, and frames finishing near their target were shown
16.7 / 25 / 33 ms apart (~200 of 300 off the grid at 40 on the iPhone). Cost:
up to one interval of extra latency when frames cannot make the next slot.

### October 28: IPA132 careers from the old Black Edition switch (GitHub issue 8)

Report: 0.4.0/0.4.1 show "NAME appears to be damaged and cannot be used" for a
career (user's `data.zip`; Stefan reproduced it with the same save). Not file
corruption: the MC02 header size, the three EA CRC32s and the trailing MD5 all
match. The first record table (file offset 0x5BCD, slot 0 = 0x12345678) has 88
slots in use with pool indices up to 85, 13 of them >= 75; Stefan's toggle-off
`MF` save uses 44, max 43. Cause (inferred from code): the pre-0.4 switch set
byte 0x82A2CE05 (see D-007); in `sub_822CBC00`'s loop, at 0x822CBD68
(`lbz r4,-12795`), CE05 != 0 makes it create an extra record
(`bl sub_822CB458`). 0.4 never sets CE05, so those records are missing when
the career loads. Fix, `ios/src/game_pool.cpp`: when the game opens a save
(save hook, Open), count slots with an index >= 75 in the file
(`Documents/data/*/454107D9/00000001/<name>/<name>`); set CE05 = 1 if any,
else 0, and log `[pool] save '...': N entries past 75 (old Black Edition
switch); byte 82A2CE05 = 0|1`. CE06 (Black Edition) is untouched. Untested
assumption: the records are built after the save is opened (if they are built
at boot, the byte comes too late and the error stays). Both bytes on together
was never run before. Built `ios/build/NFSMW-legacy-records-132.ipa`, UUID
06F495E4-2656-365D-B1BD-F177AE237DCE, SHA256 564f2a4d0787ef71..., ZIP test OK,
208 metallibs. To test: the issue 8 save loads; a toggle-off career still
loads (log shows byte = 0).

IPA132 result (Stefan, iPad, Oct 28): BEPPY loads; NAME still "damaged" although
the log shows `13 entries past 75 ... byte 82A2CE05 = 1` at its open, before
the load. Stefan's device has no `save_extras/NAME.pool` (no "wait" line for
NAME). A copy of NAME with the 13 slots >= 75 cleared (free slot pattern) and
the header recomputed, imported, is also "damaged". Offline checks of NAME, all
pass: header size, three CRC32s, trailing MD5, the gameplay section's own MD5
(0x34) and its structure (8 persistent activities, timers, types, milestones,
traps, hiding bits, bin bytes as `save_convert.cpp` parses them). So CE05 alone
and the missing overflow alone are not the cause (negative results).

### October 28: IPA133 save loader probe (temporary, D-010)

The career loader `sub_822C3A60(profile, buffer, size, r6, mode)` fails (r3 =
0) in two places: the word after the gameplay section (mode 0: where
`sub_822C2998` stopped; else buffer+16+23033) differs from word +8 of the
object at `0x82A2C684`, or `sub_822C3718` returns 0. `ios/src/game_load_probe.cpp`
wraps the three and logs `[load-probe]` lines (inputs, the compared words,
results). IPA132's CE05 change is still in. Built
`ios/build/NFSMW-load-probe-133.ipa`, UUID 4EE16A65-4732-3F06-960F-15BC4CAA9596,
SHA256 8907165e892d19a9..., ZIP test OK, 208 metallibs. Test: load NAME and
BEPPY, send the log.

IPA133 result (Stefan, iPad, Oct 28): NAME: `load -> 0 | word at buffer+23049
= 2C9B8528, game expects 55ADA3B6 (DIFFERENT)`, sub_822C3718 never reached.
BEPPY: sub_822C3718 -> 1, word 55ADA3B6 = expected, load -> 1. The word is the
ID just before the profile name (file offset 0x5A2D); Stefan's MF save from
Xenia in August has 55ADA3B6 too. Cause: the career's player ID, not Black
Edition and not damage. The gameplay section was 23033 bytes in both.

### October 28: IPA134 load careers saved under another player ID (D-010)

`ios/src/game_save_id.cpp` (replaces the probe): when `sub_822C3A60` returns 0
in mode 0 and the 4 bytes where `sub_822C2998` stopped differ from word +8 of

### October 29: 0.4.2-diag1, diagnostic build for the iOS 26 native crash (D-011)

Report (GitHub user, `.ips` and log in
`/Users/bep1s/Developer/Debug/Most Wanted (2005) Debug/29 October 2026/`):
iPhone18,2 (17 Pro Max), iOS 26.7.2 23H128, 0.4.2 build 6. EXC_BAD_ACCESS
(SIGSEGV) KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS 0x9a0 on queue `nfsmw.native`, 1-2 s after Play
(first native frames, front end loading). Top frame AGXMetalG18P
`-[AGXG18PFamilyRenderContext drawIndexedPrimitives:...] +240` (`ldr x9,
[x8,#0x9a0]`, x8 null: the driver reads an empty slot of the encoder's
state), called from `(anonymous namespace)::RenderFrame +67772` (the NativeSwap
block); the only indexed draw is the game draw in `native_renderer.mm`. Pure
Vulkan works on that phone; native works on Stefan's 17 Pro Max on iOS 27.
Cause not known.

Change (branch `diag-ios26-native-crash` off `main` 0.4.2, Stefan approved
via the coordinator, logs only, no draw skipped):
- `ios_main.mm` `StartDiagnostics`, first thing in `main()` after the
  Documents folders: opens `Documents/logs/native_diag.txt`; unless
  extra_args.txt has `--nfsmw_diag_metal_validation=false` (cvar, default
  true; read by a plain text scan, so a UTF-16 extra_args.txt is not seen),
  sets `MTL_DEBUG_LAYER=1`, `MTL_DEBUG_LAYER_ERROR_MODE=nslog`,
  `MTL_DEBUG_LAYER_WARNING_MODE=nslog` (report and continue, so the crash
  still happens), `MTL_SHADER_VALIDATION=0`, `OS_ACTIVITY_DT_MODE=YES` (NSLog
  copied to stderr) and points stderr at native_diag.txt. nfsmw.log gets a
  `[diag] D-011 diagnostic build` line with both switches.
- `native_renderer.mm`, cvar `nfsmw_diag_draw_log` (default true): for the
  first 5 frames with draws (at most 400 lines) one line per new game encoder
  (pass, encoder class, attachments: colour 0/1/4 and depth/stencil
  format/sample count/size, visibility buffer) and per game draw (index count,
  index buffer and length vs offset + count*4, pso and PipelineKey formats,
  samples, alpha spec, motion, the pass's attachments, depth-stencil state,
  visibility slot, nil vertex buffers among the shader's inputs 9..30) and
  per full-screen `drawPrimitives` (encoder, attachments). Each line is
  written with write() + fsync() before the draw. Differences are flagged
  `MISMATCH` with a name (index-overrun, c0-format, c0-samples, c1-presence,
  c1-format, c4-presence, c4-format, depth, stencil, no-depth-state,
  visibility, vertex-buffer, nil-encoder). If validation is active the encoder
  class should be an MTLDebug... wrapper instead of AGX....
- Version `0.4.2-diag1` (CFBundleShortVersionString, build 6), shown in the
  launcher and the first line of native_diag.txt.

Built `ios/build/NFS-Most-Wanted-0.4.2-diag1.ipa`, SHA-256
ec33bb733fc385adb8cab88157c40e8a64f22929316e5ec4e68f7437230c0cf2, UUID
0C78385E-6C9D-38A1-A5E8-FC03B4EFFB48, 208 metallibs, ZIP test OK, codesign --deep --strict ok. Not run on a
device yet. Unverified: whether iOS 26/27 honours MTL_DEBUG_LAYER for an app
launched without Xcode (the encoder class in native_diag.txt shows it), and

`native_diag.txt` (copy in `.../29 October 2026/diag1 Stefan iOS27/`): 157
lines, 5 frames; every game encoder is `MTLDebugRenderCommandEncoder`, so
MTL_DEBUG_LAYER is honoured without Xcode; no validation message reached the
file (none raised, or NSLog not copied to stderr: not distinguishable from
this run); 0 MISMATCH. Frame 1 drew no game draw (pipelines not ready), only
full-screen passes. All draws: triangle lists, 32-bit indices in range,
sample count 1, depth 260 (Depth32Float_Stencil8) on every pass. The
`nfsmw.log` sent with it is an older one (last start Oct 29 00:49, build
Oct 28 21:56), not from this run. Next: the GitHub user's run on iOS 26.

0.4.2-diag1 on the GitHub user's iPhone 17 Pro Max, iOS 26 (Oct 29; copies in
`.../29 October 2026/diag1 GitHub user iOS26/`): **no crash**, the game
plays, but as low as 17 fps (user; SpeedBreaker 60). Log: build Oct 29
11:24:38, validation on, draw log on, native backend, scale 1.0, MSAA off,
cap 40; `pacing: 300 of 300 frames off the 25.0 ms grid`; frame 1801: 3008
draws. native_diag.txt: 148 lines, 0 MISMATCH, no validation message,
encoders `MTLDebugRenderCommandEncoder`, attachments 1600x736.
Inference (not proven): the debug layer stands between the renderer and
AGX (it forwards every call itself and retains every object it is given),
which hides the crash; the low frame rate is that layer's CPU cost on ~3000
draws a frame, not representative. Either the crash needs AGX to receive
our calls directly (driver state bug), or an object we use is freed early
and the layer's retains keep it alive. Next: the same build with
`--nfsmw_diag_metal_validation=false` in extra_args.txt (UTF-8): draw log
only, expected to crash, the last native_diag.txt line names the draw.

0.4.2-diag1 with `--nfsmw_diag_metal_validation=false`, GitHub user, iOS
26.7.2 23H128 (Oct 29; copies in `.../29 October 2026/diag1 GitHub user iOS26
validation off/`): crashes as before (.ips: SIGSEGV 0x9a0 in AGX
`drawIndexedPrimitives` +240, RenderFrame +75648, queue nfsmw.native).
native_diag.txt ends at frame 2, draw 5 (0 MISMATCH). **Cause found:** on
iOS 26 AGX hands out every new render encoder at the same address
(frame 1: 0x10e9543f0 for all ten game passes; frame 2: 0x10e903f00). The
renderer's per-encoder caches (`EncoderState::For`, `bias_encoder`,
`visibility_encoder`) detect a new encoder by comparing that pointer, so on
iOS 26 they never reset. Draw 5 is the first draw on a new encoder whose
pipeline equals the previous draw's (draw 4 and 5: pso 0x12e3b0000), so
`setRenderPipelineState` is skipped and the new encoder draws with no
pipeline: the null state slot. (Depth state, vertex buffers 9+, depth bias
and visibility were already skipped the same way since draw 2, without a
crash.) On iOS 27, and under the debug layer, each encoder has a new
address, so the caches reset and nothing shows. Proposed fix (not made,
awaiting Stefan): at the game encoder's creation, clear the trackers
(`state.enc = nil; bias_encoder = nil; visibility_encoder = nil;`, as
`clip_mode_encoder` already is) so the reset no longer depends on the
address.

buffer, depth bias and visibility caches reset on every new encoder whatever

Minimap position fix (Oct 29, approved by Stefan). Bug: after leaving the
safe house a second time, or finishing/restarting a race, the minimap's map
and icons are drawn inward from its ring (IMG_4038; a GitHub user's
IMG_4045), also with Custom HUD off. Cause (inferred from the code, not
traced): the HUD is rebuilt, often at the old HUD's address, and its minimap
at the old minimap's address. MoveMinimap only treats a minimap as new when
its address changes or (when the game did not just switch widescreen) its
+184 differs from what was written; the new HUD's first update switches it
to widescreen, so `switched` was true, the old offset state (m.x = -extra)
was kept and the new minimap, its children and +184 got no wide-scene shift
(105 HUD units at 1560x720); the pivot (set outright by the game) was still
moved, and the ring moves with the left group. Fix (game_scene_size.cpp,
sub_822AA6D0 hook): the widescreen flag hud+816 only changes inside the
game's call, so a flag that differs from the value left after the previous
call, or another HUD address, marks a new HUD and resets g_minimap. IPA138
`ios/build/NFSMW-minimap-138.ipa` (0.4.3 + fix): SHA-256
9c2816c04f65535db4b67453eaba04651dffcd89c1b0df6a25907103a0eb4bcf, 30111768
bytes, UUID 26C71920-3AE0-3D23-89C2-B47DC4EA1492, 208 metallibs, `unzip -t`
ok, codesign --deep --strict ok. Not run on a device yet.

### October 29: touch controls step 1, steering modes (IPA151)

Stefan's plan (BACKLOG "Touch controls overhaul"), step 1, approved Oct 29.
- `touch_controls.mm`: cvar `ios_touch_steering` (dynamic / fixed /
  buttons, default dynamic) picks the DRIVE layout's steering. fixed: the
  old circle. buttons: two round buttons (◀ ▶, layout names `drive.◀`,
  `drive.▶`) that push the left stick to -1 / +1 (Control::left_x; both
  held: straight). dynamic: a horizontal stick (Control::dynamic) that
  takes any touch in the bottom-left quarter not on another control
  (added last, so nitrous and look back win), centres itself under the
  thumb (kept whole on screen), is drawn only while held, then fades out
  in 0.25 s (30 Hz timer, Control::fade). The redraw tracks each control's
  last drawn bounds so the old spot is cleared when it moves (Look() hashes
  its centre and fade). The setting is checked twice a second with the
  native-mode timer and the layout rebuilt when it changes (`[touch]
  steering: ...`).
- Editor: the dynamic joystick is not placed; its zone is outlined
  (dashed, "STEERING thumb anywhere here"). MakeLayoutEditor takes the
  launcher's touch_steering, since the cvar is only set at game start.
- Launcher: Touch controls › Steering (choice, `--ios_touch_steering`);
  in-game options: same row, live (LiveFlags).

### October 29: race/pursuit start feels low frame rate at 60 fps (logs only, no change)

Stefan: for roughly the first 20-30 s of races and pursuits (and the
transition into them) the world feels like a low frame rate while the
counter shows 60. Logs `Debug/29 October 2026/nfsmw_ipa141_pursuit_race_70pct_ipad.log`
and `nfsmw_ipa142_pursuit_70pct_ipad.log` (iPad, cap 60, Low Power Mode off,
thermal nominal). Measured:
- Display steady at 60 Hz (`[display] refresh now 60 Hz`, no change later).
- After `game flow state 6`: one load hitch (IPA142 frame 1656, 193 ms,
  327 textures decoded), then pacing 0-2 of 300 frames off the 16.7 ms grid,
  worst 8-33 ms; frame numbers advance 300 per 5 s, so the main loop runs
  at 60 and each frame is shown once, on time, from the first seconds on.
- `[cpu]` rises from 89% to 179% of a core between the first and second
  10 s of the IPA142 pursuit.
- iPad: adaptive QoS off (6 E cores), every game thread on Utility the whole
  time. iPhone logs (e.g. IPA159): adaptive boost is on from boot for 40 s
  and runs out about 19 s into the world ("back to Utility"), then returns
  after late frames: the first seconds are boosted, not slowed.
Inference (not measured): the presentation side is not the cause; what is
left is the content's motion, as in D-005 before IPA124 (frame_clock.cpp
gives the world one period per frame; raw frames >= 250 ms bypass it and a
far-off debt resyncs). QoS cannot explain the iPad case. No camera log was
on in these runs, so the world's step per frame at the start is unknown.
Proposed next (existing switches, no build): a start-of-race run with
`--nfsmw_native_camera_log=true`, then the same with `--nfsmw_frame_ticks=0`,
and on the iPad `--ios_utility_qos=false --ios_utility_qos_guest=false`.

Low Power Mode off, thermal nominal; no crash this run, a race was played).

  2868x1320. Stefan's same-size iPhone at 1x gets 1564x720.
- Performance: in the world, 0-2 of 300 frames off the grid until
  `[adaptive-qos] back to Utility` (19:47:18.6, 14.5 s into the race, the
  40 s boot boost running out). From 19:47:23: render-queue hitches of
  ~31 ms with 23-25 ms "waiting for a drawable" every other frame, then
  pacing 150 of 300 frames off the grid (gaps 2:150 4:150: alternating
  16.7 / 33.3 ms, ~40 fps shown) until he quit at 19:47:54. The boost never
  came back during those 30 s: adaptive_qos.cpp OnSwap counts late guest
  swaps on the GPU command thread, which stayed on time; the shown frames
  were the late ones. It re-boosted only on the menu.
Inference: the iPhone's adaptive QoS lets the render path drop to Utility
and its late-frame detector cannot see drops on the presentation side. Same
finding as the "back to Utility" note from the crash thread; fix belongs there.

### October 29: 0.4.3 Performance setting (Eco / Balanced / Max), QoS while driving

Stefan approved (via the coordinator) after the GitHub tester's diag2 log
(Vipe95, iPhone 17 Pro Max, iOS 26.7.2, cap 60, scale 0.85; evidence above,
commit 966d165): 60 fps while adaptive QoS was boosted, then
`[adaptive-qos] back to Utility` at 19:47:18 and 60 -> 49 -> a flat 40 fps,
rendering 15.8 -> ~23 ms/frame with GPU ~11 ms; re-boost only at 19:47:54
(`2 late frames of 120, 36 s on Utility`): a steady 40 at 1.5x the 60
budget was rarely counted late. Changes:
- `adaptive_qos.cpp`: game_state.cpp reports driving (in the world, no menu
  up) with `SetDriving`; while driving the mode is pinned boosted (main, GPU
  command thread, guest threads by override, render queue), with a 5 s hold
  after driving stops. Outside driving a frame is late when its swap interval
  is over 1.1x the cap's budget, or (`OnRendered`, from RenderFrame) its
  encoding time without the drawable wait is over the budget; 3 late frames
  in the last 60 boost (was 2 of 120 over 1.2x).
- Launcher Graphics option "Performance" (`performance_mode`: eco /
  balanced / max; default balanced, eco when Battery mode is on and nothing
  was chosen; a choice wins). `--nfsmw_performance_mode` and
  `--nfsmw_performance_source` (setting / battery_mode / default).
  `ApplyUtilityQosDefault` (ios_main.mm) now sets, unless Extra Args name them:
  Balanced: ios_utility_qos false, ios_utility_qos_guest true,
  ios_adaptive_qos true, nfsmw_native_render_utility true (adaptive on every
  device; the iPads' fixed Utility for main/GPU threads, default with >= 6
  efficiency cores since Oct 21, is gone, so iPad battery may differ: not
  measured). Max: all four false (no Utility). Eco: ios_utility_qos true,
  guest true, adaptive false, render utility true, and the on-demand pipeline
  compile queue at Utility (was User Initiated). Not changed in any mode:
  CoreAudio's RemoteIO thread and the real-time vblank thread
  (`ios_vblank_realtime`), so no crackles, voice cuts or pacing loss.
- Log: nfsmw.log `[performance] <mode> (<source>): ...`, boot.txt
  `performance: <mode> (<source>)`; `[adaptive-qos] driving: boosted until
  driving stops`, `[adaptive-qos] User Initiated (driving)`, `[adaptive-qos]
  driving stopped: Utility allowed again`, late boosts now say `of 60`.
- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/performance.yml` (new) and `bug_report.yml` (new,
  with a Performance report section): device, iOS, install method, version,
  settings including Performance, Low Power Mode, nfsmw.log from a run with a
  race, FPS counter screenshots.

Proposed an isolated default-off 40-only CAMetalDisplayLink experiment.
Stefan selected "Review the design first": NO 40 source edits authorized
by that response; no experiment code/build made. Review design:
1. Attach Metal display link to primary layer only under a new test flag
   and effective cap 40. Keep existing CADisplayLink/guest 120 Hz timing,
   even world-frame time and simulation intact.
2. On system callbacks, pass the supplied drawable + presentation timestamp
   to the existing serial native renderer via a bounded handoff. Acquire
   before encoding each experimental frame, rather than late nextDrawable;
   never render/wait on the main thread. One frame per callback, preserve
   ordering, existing in-flight limit, resource/writeback lifetimes.
3. Present against system timing, not the old EMA GPU-time+4 ms target
   grid. Start with bounded/default two-frame latency, measure actual
   input-to-display/queue latency (possible tradeoff; not guaranteed lower).
4. Lifecycle/cap switch: invalidate/pause link and wake waits on background,
   layer loss or leave-40; discard stale updates with a generation marker.
   Never acquire from nextDrawable while the Metal display link owns that
   layer's acquisition. Restore legacy acquisition only after handoff is
   stopped. 30/menu transition, 60/120 and external-display legacy paths
   preserved; off switch restores current implementation.
5. Logs: active path, callback cadence, system target, missed deadlines,
   acquisition/queue wait; retain existing frame trace for comparable

Source/API investigation found a concrete defect introduced by this
experiment: its managed-drawable branch called
[cb presentDrawable:drawable atTime:system_target]. Apple explicitly warns
that time-targeted presentation methods assert with CAMetalDisplayLink:
https://developer.apple.com/documentation/quartzcore/cametaldisplaylinkdelegate/metaldisplaylink(_:needsupdate:)
Strong match to startup termination around initial presentation, but no
.ips/boot.txt supplied to prove these exact crash stacks. Correcting a
known API violation is justified without claiming stack-level confirmation.

Corrected managed branch uses plain [cb presentDrawable:drawable], which
calls drawable.present after Metal schedules the rendering buffer. This
preserves GPU-write dependencies; never call atTime or minimumDuration on
system-supplied drawables. targetPresentationTimestamp now diagnostic only.
Apple plain drawable API and scheduling recommendation:
https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/mtldrawable/present()
Apple commit/present deadline is targetTimestamp, not the later estimated
targetPresentationTimestamp:
https://developer.apple.com/documentation/quartzcore/cametaldisplaylink/update/targettimestamp
Stale update filtering corrected to use targetTimestamp. Added scheduled-
handler deadline diagnostics, protected against concurrent callbacks.
Existing 30/60/120, game/QoS behavior and default-off test flag unchanged.

(exit 0, ios/build/metal-display-40-plain-present-build.log), but was not

Correction (experimental managed40 driving only):
- New pure C++ ManagedFrameSlots in managed_frame_slots.h. On each render
  frame's acquired system drawable, account elapsed assigned system target
  slots beyond the one normal frame. Use current managed full-frame period.
  Collect only across driving frames; reset on menu,stop/start,invalid/
  nonmonotonic/long(>=10slot) discontinuities. Protected by existing pacer
  mutex; no new callbacks/frame ordering or GPU lifetime changes.
- Fractional excess target intervals carried across assignments. Avoid
  rounding individual gaps:1.5-slot/.5-slot phase jitter cancels rather
  than inventing a missed frame. Small1e-6-slot arithmetic tolerance.
- Bounded pending12slots. Clock takes at most9missing slots/update (maximum
  managed step250ms at nominal40),remaining debt retained. This covers
  modeled5fps as well as normal30/20/10; existing>=250ms loading bypass
  still returns original elapsed time and clears missed-slot history.
  Original modes/menus/other caps unchanged. At steady40 no missing slots,
  same full-step behavior that Stefan accepted in log9. Feedback arrives
  from render assignment and is consumed in later game updates,so brief
  bounded time lag is expected; this is not exact same-frame correction.
- display_rate exposes TakeManagedMissedSlots to C++ clock via pacer.
  [world-missed] reports compensated slots per300 driving updates when
  world logger enabled. Keep existing world-clock6-value format. Frame
  trace counter budget increased400->800 (still default-off) to retain
  later settings/heavy-chase phases. No new test arguments/default change.

changes, binaries launched, sockets/server started, device tests, pushes or releases.

full filenames and next action in this branch's checkpoint. Main remains on main.

are pinned upstream commits and this committed record.

Sources actually inspected:
- Local sibling NFSMW-Recompiled-Mobile HEAD `b61e4bf` (README says multiplayer
  not working; diary wrongly proposes System Link). Do not use that as current
  Android multiplayer evidence. Remote upstream was verified through web search
  and fresh shallow clone, without updating the sibling reference.
- https://github.com/victorgbd/NFSMW-Recompiled-Mobile/tree/d534be88edf5bcd362445c84e5b79c61e29571e7
  snapshot `/private/tmp/nfsmw-multiplayer-upstream`. Read current README/release
  notes, docs/diario/red-y-privilegios.md, tools/red/README.md;
  nativo/sdk/src/kernel/xam/{xam_net.cpp,xam_user.cpp,apps/xlivebase_app.cpp,
  apps/xgi_app.cpp}, nativo/sdk/src/system/xsocket.cpp;
  nativo/app/src/nfsmw_red_sonda.cpp; Android MotorNativo/hosting references;
  ios/motor/{red_lan.h,red_lan.cpp,servidor_ea.cpp,lanzador.mm,segundo_plano.mm},
  ios/README.md and USA address table.
- https://github.com/victorgbd/nfsmw-server-lan/tree/821b9b54cf1ded01ffe2e3fd05c38b7c4c906da6
  snapshot `/private/tmp/nfsmw-server-lan-research`; README and ea_server.py.
- Apple local-network privacy:
  https://developer.apple.com/documentation/technotes/tn3179-understanding-local-network-privacy
  and broadcast/multicast entitlement:
  https://developer.apple.com/documentation/bundleresources/entitlements/com.apple.developer.networking.multicast

Observed upstream method and evidence limits:
1. Xbox 360 Most Wanted has no System Link per upstream's actual menu/log
   investigation. It revives the Xbox Live menu using a local replacement for
   EA's 2005 DirtySock/Aries services. Earlier diary sections remain historical
   and contradict the newer correction near its top. XSessionSearch broadcast
   emulation alone is the wrong starting point for this game.
2. Server directory TCP30960 -> lobby TCP10901; lobby messages use a12-byte
   header (4-byte command,4-byte subcode, big-endian total length), newline
   key=value body terminated by NUL, product nfs-xbox-2006. Login/auth/persona,
   room create/search/join, member lists (+usm), game records, start/results and
   heartbeat (~png every20s) are implemented. Correct user-set membership and
   per-peer addresses/XUIDs matter; generic success stubs cannot replace them.
3. Actual race is DirtySock ConnApi/CommUDP between phones on UDP3658; server
   doesn't relay/translate racing data. README lists UDP6000 for voice; voice
   operation was not independently verified here. Upstream diary reports a full
   circuit, both result submissions and host-role switch on October16 between
   RedMagic SM8750 and Galaxy A22; release0.5.0 names Snapdragon8Elite/A22 and
   PAL Spain. These are upstream reports, not new tests on Stefan's port.
4. Android can host the same lobby using ServidorEa.java in a foreground service;
   Python ea_server.py on a PC is equivalent. A PC hosting this service is NOT
   evidence the original Windows game can join. Launcher discovery UDP10902
   sends NFSMW_DISCOVER and receives NFSMW_SERVER/NAME/PLAYERS. TCP10902 checks
   GAMERTAG with FREE/IN_USE and reserves names. Host advertises its LAN IP,
   not127.0.0.1. Distinct gamertags and per-device runtime XUIDs avoid collisions.
5. Selecting server enables grant_user_privileges,red_lan,red_live,red_dns;
   red_registro is diagnostic. red_live reports signed-in state2; red_lan exposes
   actual LAN IP/link status; red_dns redirects game DNS/EA service lookup to
   replacement host. XOnlineGetServiceInfo(0x45410004) must return that endpoint.
6. Missing XNet keys/connect/QoS/session information are supplied in the LAN
   context. Socket fixes include nonblocking FIONBIO, host-option translation,
   errno->WSA errors, select nfds, byte order, getsockname/getpeername/getsockopt,
   overlapped receiving/completion and events. In particular WSAWaitForMultipleEvents
   must invert WinSock wait_all into kernel wait type, convert milliseconds to
   negative relative100ns units, and return actual event index/timeout. Original
   behavior can receive the first peer packet and then stop.
7. Essential behavioral hook is in misleadingly named nfsmw_red_sonda.cpp:
   PAL sub_82829AD0 bypasses DirtySock's catch-all xmap for non127 peer addresses,
   while retaining loopback->EA service mapping. Without it UDP intended for a
   friend goes to the lobby host instead. Other hooks in that file are diagnostic.
   Our port is USA: no match for82829AD0/82819F48 in upstream USA TSV during this
   inspection. This does not prove equivalents absent; map by game code/call
   semantics before use. Do not transplant hard-coded PAL addresses blindly.

Integration assessment (inferences/planned work, NOT implemented):
- Android/iOS compatibility is plausible because both execute the same360 engine
  and could use unchanged lobby/CommUDP protocols. Preserve Android wire format
  and join its existing host first. Edition/version/content compatibility is an
  open test gate: upstream evidence is PAL Spain, our target USA. A successful
  lobby does not prove race loading, car/track IDs or simulation agreement.
- Our SDK currently returns loopback XNADDR, link down, conversion errors and
  placeholder strings, plus mostly no-op XGI sessions. grant_user_privileges
  already exists defaultfalse. Relevant local files mirror upstream integration
  points, but are part of extensively patched SDK. Port scoped changes as
  reproducible tools/ios preparation patches on isolated SDK source/build paths;
  avoid applying a broad upstream SDK replacement to shared active controls work.
- Darwin requires careful sockaddr layout/length and socket-option translation.
  Upstream generic POSIX socket code uses MSG_NOSIGNAL; adapt/verify Apple
  SO_NOSIGPIPE and cancellation/socket lifetime behavior rather than assuming
  Android code compiles/behaves identically. Reuse existing SDK object ownership.
- Our Info.plist.in lacks NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription; custom broadcast
  discovery needs entitlement/access handling. App entitlements do not control
  LiveContainer's process: verify its permission and signed host entitlements on
  actual devices. First milestone manual server IP + unicast avoids depending on
  discovery. Add clear network error state and disabled-by-default LAN mode.
- Upstream already has a C++ iOS lobby and synthetic protocol-comparison tests.
  Its iOS README explicitly says launcher/LAN hosting features untested on an
  iPhone, despite broad README claims. Useful reference, not proof for our Metal
  port. Its background server uses looping silent audio; no approval to import
  that audio/lifecycle behavior into this port. Prefer foreground hosting first
  and test background/disconnect/rejoin deliberately later.

PC conclusion: shared lobby concepts give a reason to investigate, not a proven
cross-play path. Native PC LAN discovery/lobby may differ from360 online flow;
start by capturing PC<->PC LAN create/join/start traffic, separately compare PC
online Aries flow if accessible. Then compare transport handshake, packet types,
reliability/framing, field byte order (x86 vs PPC), IDs and race state encoding
against Android<->Android. Determine whether (a) direct wire compatibility,
(b) lobby/discovery adapter only, or (c) ongoing race-payload translator / PC-side
mod is required. No evidence yet rules any of these in/out. Lobby server cannot
fix race payload mismatches because races bypass it. Do not promise unmodified
PC LAN interoperability or estimate this as a simple server-IP setting.

  uses selected server instead of public DNS. New XNet LAN operations fail when

  observed0x5000D game-start is acknowledged in LAN mode. Runtime XUID derives
  from LAN IP as upstream; stored profile/content/save XUID unchanged.

  identified via neighboring mapped functions' -0x1f0 displacement, then actual
  generated function reviewed: reads r4 address bytes4..7, walks {address,mask,
  replacement}12-byte table, copies16-byte socket address to r3 and writes the
  replacement IP. Called from two socket paths (generated .52/.84). This
  substantiates function identity; not merely an assumed constant shift.
  With red_lan and non127 address, returns original pointer directly; loopback
  retains original service mapping. Non-LAN mode calls original import.
- Launcher Game section: LAN mode Off(default)/Join/Host, server address and
  gamertag. Preflight on background queue resolves endpoint, starts foreground
  host if selected, checks gamertag/unreachable server; failure returns error
  before game launch. Host shows real LAN address, never127.0.0.1. Unique names
  required. Uses upstream flags; preview network logging on. Other Extra Args
  override as usual. NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription added. No broadcast
  discovery UI, multicast entitlement, silent background audio, rendering,

  LR82829FE4. That callee saves r27 at receiverSP-48 (same descriptor slot).
  r27 is global socket-list address0x829118D0 (sign-extended64bits). Old worker
  can therefore read lenFFFFFFFF, destination829118D0, and overwrite21bytes
  of global network state. Packet prefix00000100 becomes listhead0x100;
  receiver loads listnode+96 => read0x160, exactly both logged faults.
  Scheduling of overwrite was not captured directly, but alias, packet bytes,
  resulting pointer/fault, and deterministic regression corroborate this cause.
- Thread getter8262EA20 reads PCR+100 then thread+14C; not the0x160 access.
  Existing stack-top256-byte pad is unrelated and unchanged. No AV swallowing,
  null-list workaround, game logic bypass or changed synchronization.

Source/interpretation:
- Actual USA CommUDP sub_8289C448 calls DirtySock SocketRecvfrom8282A5A0 at
  LR8289C4D8, then reads its two32bit header fields as big-endian guest words.
  Captured PC bytes therefore become0x05000000/0xC5B964C6 to Xbox; interpreting
  PC words little-endian yields5/0xC664B9C5. Xbox TX1 is written big-endian.
  Opposite header byte order is a concrete wire difference and a testable
  hypothesis, not proof that swapping it completes the handshake. Connection
  identifiers/opcodes and NFS application packets may differ too.
- DirtySock SocketSendto8282A4F0 is synchronous: original path maps destination
  then calls82810E58/native sendto and returns. Captured LR8289C7B4 is CommUDP.
  SocketRecvfrom8282A5A0 dequeues completed data before returning; transforming
  at that boundary avoids changing the working asynchronous kernel receiver.
- Primary local generated code and captured traffic used. Internet searches
  for CommUDP protocol source yielded no useful primary result; no external
  CommUDP source or unsupported opcode semantics imported/claimed.

  sockets retain actual source IP; no loopback relay masquerading as the PC.

## November 1 — preview17: automatic LAN and mixed PC/mobile rooms (Claude)

Stefan asked for a simpler flow: the lobby should start automatically when the
game wants to host and join automatically otherwise, PC compatibility should not
need a separate option, and PCs should be able to play with iOS/Android players.
He approved (A) automatic hosting/joining, (B1) PCs and phones in one hosted
room and (B2) per-peer PC race translation on iOS. He cut (B3) relaying
PC↔Android race traffic, because the Android build cannot be changed here.

Design and why:
- The game's lobby address is a launch-time flag (`--red_dns`), so in the new
  `auto` mode it is always 127.0.0.1 and an in-app relay listens on
  127.0.0.1:30960 (`pc::StartAuto`). The host-or-join choice is made when the
  game first connects there, i.e. at in-game Xbox Live sign-in, which comes
  before Create Game / Quick Match. That is the earliest point the game says it
  wants multiplayer; it cannot be deferred to Create Game.
- Decision (`lan_session.cpp`, `Auto::Decide`): UDP discovery, then the TCP
  directory sweep only if UDP found nothing (`BuscarServidores(..., true)`).
  A mobile lobby wins over a PC host; ties go to the lowest address. Mobile
  lobby: the relay pipes the directory bytes unchanged and the game reaches the
  host's lobby port directly, exactly as with the old Join. PC host: the
  existing adapted gateway path runs for this connection. Nothing found: start
  the lobby with PC support on the LAN address, wait 0.3–1 s, look again, and
  if a lower address is now hosting with nobody in this lobby, stop and join
  it. Follow-up connections within 20 s reuse the decision (a PC host's lobby
  reconnects through the relay). A host with players keeps hosting on re-sign-in.
- Discovery marks a host as a PC only if it answers TCP9900 but not the mobile
  directory, because iOS hosts now also answer 9900. Manual Join by address
  checks the mobile directory before the PC probe for the same reason.
- Unified lobby (B1): `ArrancarPC` no longer rejects mobile guests, answers the
  mobile UDP search, and accepts up to three PC guests (`SetHostingPeer`). The
  directory port binds to the LAN address so 127.0.0.1:30960 stays free for the
  relay. Per-recipient translation (`HostReply`) was already per session.
- iOS guests learn which room members are PCs with a new `PCPEERS` question on
  the existing gamertag port 10902, polled once a second while joined.
  Android and older hosts answer ERROR, which means no PCs.
- Per-peer race state (B2): `pc_gateway.cpp` keeps up to three PC peers, each
  with its own remote/local CommUDP IDs and role. A hosted PC guest is a
  listener peer (unchanged), a manually joined PC host is a connector peer
  (unchanged), and peers from `PCPEERS` learn the role from the first INIT
  (received ⇒ listener, sent ⇒ connector), since between two guests either side
  may connect first. `game_pc_udp.cpp` uses `Hosting(ip)`/`NoteInit` instead of
  the global hosting flag.
- Known limits: car setup fields switch to PC byte order on every iOS device
  that knows about a PC (`pc::Active()`), so all iOS devices in that room agree.
  Android cannot, so Android and PC players cannot race in the same room (the
  launcher says so). Up to ~8 s of discovery happens while the game waits for
  its directory reply; the game's timeout for that is not measured. Two devices
  signing in in the same second rely on the UDP re-check; if UDP replies are
  blocked on that network both may end up hosting (sign out and in again).
- UI: Multiplayer now offers “Play on this Wi-Fi” (automatic) and “Join by
  address”. Host, Join search and Host for PCs are no longer shown; their code
  paths (`host`, `host_pc`, `join`) remain for manual join and older settings.

Verification (all from /private/tmp/nfsmw-ios-multiplayer):
- `python3 tools/ios/test_lan_setup.py`: existing preflight plus automatic
  decisions (mobile preferred over PC, reuse within one sign-in, PC join, host
  when alone, higher address yields to a simultaneous lower host).
- `python3 tools/ios/test_pc_udp.py` (ASan/UBSan): existing captures plus role
  learned from first received/sent INIT.
- `python3 tools/ios/test_pc_gateway.py` (ASan/UBSan): three hosted PCs with
  separate IDs and cap, guest list keeps surviving IDs, first INIT fixes role.
- `python3 tools/ios/test_pc_host.py --sdk /private/tmp/nfsmw-multiplayer-sdk

- Not tested: any real device, relay timing against the game's directory

## November 1 — preview18: refresh the PC's room count (Claude)

Stefan approved the proposed fix for the PC room list missing later joiners.
`servidor_ea.cpp` `avisarSalaPC`: after `ujoi` and `ulea`, the host resends the
room record (`+ust`, translated by `HostReply` like every PC reply) to PC
sessions subscribed to that room, so their player count C follows joins and
leaves. Sent only to PCs: phones already repair the count client-side and

still don't decrement C (pre-existing behavior, unchanged). Answer to Stefan's
question: guests racing only through the host is expected game behavior.

### November 1: prototype debug flags matched to the USA build (dev3)

Stefan suggested using the PAL prototype to find USA addresses. Method
(scripts in the session scratchpad, not kept): the decrypted prototype image
is the loaded layout at 0x82000000 (.text from 0x820F0000, .pdata at file
0xB9600, 23405 functions). Menu labels' lis/addi references lead to the widget
setup (widget +0x14 name, +0x20 callback, +0x24 variable); variable
references give the prototype readers; each reader's function (from .pdata)
was matched to a USA generated function by mnemonic sequence (difflib on

instruction aligned by matching blocks gives the USA variable:

### November 2: context-aware keyboard keys and key prompts (dev12)

1. Two bind sets. launcher.mm KeyBind gains `menu_standard`; settings keep
   `kb_<cvar>` (driving) and new `kbm_<cvar>` (menus); the keyboard screen has
   Driving and Menus sections. Driving defaults change: A (handbrake) Space
   only (was Return,Space), B Alt (was Backspace,Alt), Start Escape,P, menu
   up/down unbound while driving. Menu defaults: arrows/WASD move, Return/
   Space/NumpadEnter = A, Escape/Backspace = B, Q/PgUp and E/PgDn = LB/RB, [ ]
   = LT/RT, Tab = Y, P = Start. The menu set goes to the game as
   `--nfsmw_menu_keybinds=keybind_a=...;...`. `keyboard_context.cpp` keeps both
   and assigns the SDK's `keybind_*` strings (REXCVAR_DECLARE'd storage) on
   each menu/driving change from game_state.cpp (same change as
   battery::SetInMenu). The SDK driver reads those strings on its input
   thread: each gets 256 bytes reserved and values are cut to 255, so an
   assignment never reallocates (a poll can see a torn list, not freed
   memory; inference from libc++ assign semantics, not tested under load). A
   switch waits until no key is down (polled on the main thread, 20 Hz), with
   all binds empty meanwhile, so a held Escape cannot open and close the pause
   menu. No SDK change.
2. Key prompts. `nfsmw_menu_hints_list()` (game_scene_size.cpp) exports the
   touch scan's hint icons with a known button; game_state.cpp fills them
   every 6th frame while prompts are wanted (in a menu, keyboard used last).
   `keyboard_prompts.mm`: a non-interactive UIView over the game window draws a
   key cap (first key of the menu bind for that button, e.g. Enter, Esc, ⌫,
   PgUp) over each icon, positioned with the menu-tap mapping (480 / 0.92
   tall from the screen centre). Last device wins: GCKeyboard anyKeyPressed
   shows them; a GCController button/stick or a touch (new
   nfsmw::touch::TouchesSoFar counter) hides them. Logged as
   `[keyboard] prompts on/off` and `[keyboard] menu/driving keys`.

### November 2: mouse look assessment; SDK patch for the vertical axis

Stefan: the game does not capture the Magic Keyboard's pointer, which sticks
at the screen edge. Found: the SDK already has mouse look (`mnk_mouse`,
`mnk_sensitivity`): it asks SDL for relative mode, which SDL's iOS backend
turns into iPadOS pointer lock (SDL_uikitviewcontroller.m prefersPointerLocked)
with GameController mouse deltas, and adds the deltas to the right stick
(only while `SetMouseLookActive(true)`). The launcher never turned
`mnk_mouse` on, hence a free pointer. But NFSMW has no look-around action
while driving: the game's camera actions are CHANGE, LOOKBACK, PULLBACK,
DEBUG, ENABLE_ICE (prototype strings), and the right stick's up/down shifts
gear. So mouse look while driving needs a camera hook of our own (as the PC

### November 2: resolve swap instead of resolve copies (dev31, off by default)

Native run (dev30, iPhone, 2933x1320, 14 GPU profiles): the main pass
averaged 11.70 ms (max 50.55), resolve copies 1.57 ms (18 blits), depth
copies ~1.1 ms, present 0.88 ms; the worst frame (20.91 ms) had 1.66 ms of
resolve copies. Change: `--nfsmw_native_resolve_swap=true` (default false,
for A/B in Extra arguments). A colour resolve of a whole target (rectangle
from 0,0 the size of the target's texture and of the destination, no crop,
no exponent-bias draw) takes the target's colour texture as the resolved
texture; the target gets a texture of the same descriptor from the GPU pool
(the old one is adopted into the pool so it retires like any resolve).
`Target::swapped_from` keeps the taken texture: later resolves of the target
read it; a pass that loads the target (1 sample) copies it back first ("blit:
swap restore"), a clearing pass or an MSAA pass drops it; before a kept
resolve texture retires, a target still pointing at it is copied back. Off
with the dump. Log: `[native] resolve swap: frame N, S swapped, R copied back`
every 300 frames. Expected: up to the 1.6 ms of copies less per frame where
the restores are few; not yet measured on the device.

### November 2: where a native frame's GPU time goes (smooth lap) and the options

`dev33_time_profile_last_session.log`, a 14.23 ms native frame (iPhone):
main scene pass 6.89; second scene pass d47c (composite/post) 1.55 (2);
resolve copies 1.13 (18); six cube faces 1.08 (fixed 320x256); shadow map
0.94 (fixed 1600); present 0.75; reflection pass 800 (1466x660) 0.51; depth
copies 0.79; bloom/blur chain passes 400/240/80 (733x330, 440x165, 147x117)
0.54. About 11.8 ms scales with the resolution. Earlier shader work
(Oct 21-24 cost probe, half-precision analysis) found the main pass's cost
in fill, foliage overdraw and fetches rather than arithmetic.
Options (proposed, not implemented): A, no visual change: the final picture
is resolved (copied) and then copied again to the screen by the present
pass, so presenting from the target itself where nothing else reads that
resolve, and tiled instead of linear destinations for cropped resolves
(~0.5-1 ms together, estimate). B, slight softening: the bloom/blur chain
and the reflection pass kept at 1x instead of the native scale (~0.5-0.7 ms,
estimate). C, the main pass's foliage overdraw (larger project). A + B
~1.5 ms of ~14 (~10-15%): not the halving native / 120 needs.

### November 2: tiled cropped resolves and small targets at 1x (dev34)

Stefan chose options A and B in one build. Implemented (both default on,
switches for A/B):
- `nfsmw_native_tiled_crops`: a cropped colour or depth resolve (its
  rectangle short of the destination pitch, e.g. the scene's 1560 x 704 in a
  1568 pitch) whose address the frame samples at one size that holds the
  whole rectangle goes to a private (tiled) texture of that size, sampled at
  its own size, instead of a linear texture over a buffer with a cropped
  view. Other cases (several sizes, not sampled this frame) stay linear.
- `nfsmw_native_small_targets_1x`: above 1x, when the frame has a colour
  target 1280+ wide, colour targets up to 800 wide (bloom/blur chain 400,
  240, 80; the 800 reflection pass) are drawn at 1x; resolves carry their
  scale, so sampling is unchanged. Possible side effect: other small targets
  (e.g. in menus) also at 1x.
- Not done from A: presenting from the target to skip the final copy (the
  final resolve's texture may be read again; needs checking first).
Log: `[native] resolves: frame N, T cropped ones to tiled textures ...`
every 300 frames. Build OK, not run on a device.

dev35: the scene is the frame's widest colour target 640+ wide, and targets

480, 240, 160, 80 beside 960).

Untested source leads (hypotheses, not fixes):

- Pass-counter sampling itself: native_renderer.mm creates four shared
  MTLCounterSampleBuffers and attaches start-vertex/end-fragment timestamps
  to passes and start/end timestamps to blits. `profile` is enabled EVERY
  eligible frame while hitch_lines_left > 0, otherwise every 300th; the
  samples are only READ/reported periodically or on hitches. None of the
  November 2 experiments disables this path. Same-build comparisons do not
  exclude an instrumentation/driver interaction. No evidence yet that
  counters cause D-017; this is a cheap, distinct falsifiable test.
- Residency coverage/timing: the only residency::Apply is near RenderFrame
  entry, BEFORE pooled frame buffers, targets, decoded textures and geometry
  buffers can be created and queued with residency::Add during encoding.
  These additions reach the set on the next frame. Visibility ring buffers
  and touch/FPS overlay textures also are not explicitly added to that set.
  Existing Metal resource binding/declarations can still make resources
  accessible; this is not proof of invalid access. It does mean the request-
  once experiment did not test complete coverage before first use, and CPU
  host_statistics64 paging deltas do not measure GPU mappings/wiring or
  driver waits. Some stalls have zero new vertex buffers/uploads, so newly
  created geometry alone cannot explain all of them (Max: 20/80 GPU hitch
  lines have zero new vertex buffers; reboot: 11/33). Audit coverage before
  proposing a residency correction; do not rerun the failed request-once A/B.
- Callback/backpressure: FrameLeft releases the game only after writebacks,
  counter resolution/calibration and formatted logging in its completion
  handler. A callback delay can affect following frames even though it
  cannot explain already elapsed GPU time by itself. The 50 ms NativeSwap
  wait timeout is another possible secondary amplifier, not an established
  origin. Avoid diagnosing this from CPU averages in a smooth recording.

External primary references checked November 2:
[Apple counter profiling](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/tech-talks/10001/)
describes separate vertex/fragment timing and overlapping stages;
[requestResidency](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/mtlresidencyset/requestresidency())
and [residency-set guide](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/simplifying-gpu-resource-management-with-residency-sets)
describe committed allocations, command-buffer commit and advance residency
requests; [Apple GPU performance-state tools](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2021/10157/?time=558)
describes induced states, but that is NOT proof these recordings induced one.

### November 2: dev37 bounded GPU timeline; approved diagnostic ready

Stefan approved the submission/GPU/callback/presentation timeline proposal.
New restart-only Extra Arg `--nfsmw_native_gpu_timeline=true`, default false.
No new GPU commands/counter samples, quality changes or scheduling/residency
policy changes. Existing Apply/requestResidency, command-buffer commits,
FrameLeft/visibility callback ordering and NativeSwap wait are unchanged.
A scheduled callback, small history locks/timestamps, two pending-residency
count snapshots and a bounded asynchronous logging queue are added only when
enabled; these have diagnostic overhead and could perturb timing. They are
not asserted to be free or equivalent to an uninstrumented power measurement.

Implementation:
- `ios/src/native_gpu_timeline.h`: mutex-protected 128-frame ring. Updates can
  arrive out of order; an old callback cannot overwrite a newer frame sharing
  its slot. Missing timestamps stay zero and print `-`; overwritten/missing
  whole samples are omitted. At most 12 reports per process, coalesced to at
  least eight frame numbers apart, each containing four preceding frames,
  the trigger and three following frames. Snapshot is taken from encode entry
  once four more frames have reached encoding; very late callback/presentation
  data may still be missing. No guarantee of a report if quitting before the
  four following encodes or if the budget was exhausted.
- Driving-only triggers, evaluated once frame release is recorded: final
  command-buffer GPU span >45 ms, GPU end→completion arrival >20 ms,
  commit call >20 ms, swap→encode >30 ms, or encode→commit >30 ms. No trigger
  solely for sustained 18–20 ms GPU work. Default-off leaves these probes
  inactive (the small static history storage still exists).
- `native_renderer.mm`: records swap enqueue, encode entry, final commit
  before/after, scheduled-handler host arrival, final GPUStartTime/GPUEndTime,
  completion-handler host arrival, time immediately AFTER FrameLeft, and
  drawable presentedTime. It does not move release/query handlers or wait for
  logging. Formatting/output uses separate serial Utility queue after copying
  a report outside the ring lock, max 12 x (header + 8 rows) plus enable line.
- Counts: pending residency ADD/REMOVE vector entries at encode entry and
  before final commit; new pooled objects during encoding, newly uploaded
  persistent vertex buffers, texture uploads, early-commit count and
  in-flight count at encode entry. These are not total allocation bytes or
  unique resource counts; pending lists can include other-thread additions.
  Entry snapshot is before pool reclaim/Apply, not a transactional snapshot
  of exactly what Apply consumes. Counts do not prove GPU residency or faults.

Log decoding: `[gpu-timeline] trigger N emitted from encode M origin X s`
followed by up to eight rows. Each row's ten slash-separated offsets in ms
relative to the SAME origin are:
`swap/encode/commit-in/commit-out/scheduled-callback/gpu-start/gpu-end/complete-callback/released/shown`.
Origin/times use the existing CACurrentMediaTime/Metal host-time domain.
Scheduled callback arrival is NOT the exact GPU schedule time; compare with
GPUStartTime separately, allowing callback delivery after GPU work starts.
GPU span is FINAL command buffer only; keep early commit false for this test.
`released` is after FrameLeft, not after the later visibility handler.
Compare preceding frame GPU end/release with current commit/GPU start to
account for queue backlog. Negative callback/presentation ordering differences
can be legitimate; absent data is unknown, not a zero-duration event.

  adjacent-trigger coalescing and 12-report budget, ring wrap/late callbacks,

  not actual Metal callback ordering/performance or device stutter.

Read-only optimization audit after the new instruction:

1. Concrete next CPU/upload candidate: native_renderer.mm currently allocates
   `uint32_t shared[256] = {}` per draw and `last_shared[256]`, memcmp/copies
   their full 1024 bytes, and puts 1024-byte shared blobs on changes. Budget
   sizing also reserves 1024+256 per draw regardless of actual shared upload.
   This block contains texture/sampler indices and flags, distinct from the
   VS/PS float constant banks (do NOT shrink those).
   `tools/xenosrecomp/shader_common.h` non-GTA4 layout uses 80 descriptor words
   [0,320), then flags/clip/alpha/etc through uint at offset 380: defined ABI
   fits 384 bytes/96 words. `textureDescriptorByteOffset` in translator uses
   dimension*descriptorCount+slot; NFS has 16 slots, five arrays. Renderer
   writes through word 93, reserved remaining words stay zero. Internal movie
   shader in native_renderer.mm uses descriptor words 0–2 and 64–66, also
   within this prefix. No current renderer write uses words 96–255.
   Inference: a guarded 384-byte path can remove 640 unused bytes from logical
   clear/compare/copy per block; repeated shared uploads shrink 62.5% before
   256-byte alignment (a shared allocation's following aligned offset can
   shrink from 1024 to 512). The actual benefit in CPU ms/DRAM/energy remains
   UNMEASURED. Do not equate logical bytes with measured bus traffic or claim
   GPU shading work becomes cheaper: shaders already only read their fields.
   Latest log reports ~0.62–1.09 MiB/frame shared payload in several driving
   windows; proportional reduction would be ~0.39–0.68 MiB/frame of logical
   payload at matching distinct-set counts. Budget/pool capacity might fall
   but must be observed, not promised.
   Proposed implementation, NOT YET APPROVED: independent restart-only switch
   default false for first trial; keep field offsets and 256-byte alignment,
   initialize/compare/copy/upload only 384 active bytes when enabled, update
   BOTH sizing traversals and actual upload coherently, keep 1024-byte fallback.
   Validate all defined ABI readers including clip, motion/jitter, debug movie
   paths and packaged shader compatibility; actual generated shader source
   cache is absent, so distinguish current translator ABI review from a full
   inspection of all precompiled libraries. Host prefix/packing/size tests,
   then user visual/correctness check, then matched cost/energy work if sound.
   No shader arithmetic, image content or scheduling changes proposed here.
2. CPU follow-up (previously proposed, not already tested/implemented): new
   pass rebuilds a flattened array from textures/resolved_textures/
   assembled_cubes/volumes/cubes, then dummy_array/data, for every encoder.
   A frame-local cache invalidated on collection growth could retain the SAME
   list/order and SAME useResources call per encoder, avoiding repeated ObjC
   enumeration. Historical TECHNICAL sections around the lazy-diagnostics and
   upload-sizing audits already identify this opportunity, not a measured
   experiment. Do not remove residency/hazard declarations as a shortcut.
   More aggressive per-pass actual-read lists need separate shader/binding
   liveness proof and CPU cost evidence; not in first change.
3. GPU: main-scene cost (~half the smooth native frame) remains the largest
   target. Re-read October 21 cost probe and October 24 half-precision audit:
   top foliage/cutout shaders involve fetch/overdraw, not large removable
   arithmetic. New hypothesis to verify, NOT an established optimization:
   the translator's generic alpha test is emitted at return, so where final
   alpha is provably known earlier, reject transparent pixels before expensive
   colour/shadow work. Need actual shader dependency/derivative/LOD/control-
   flow analysis and matching alpha/depth/blend results; cannot assume this
   helps the already-cheap one-fetch tree shader, or force early depth in a
   discard shader. No broad fp16/fast-math or fidelity reduction proposed.
   Historical source paths `.../shaders/air/ps_684f....metal` and 27d82ea0
   no longer exist on this restored machine: cache currently has lib/ only.
   Read-only targeted search found libraries/capture PNGs but no matching
   generated .metal/.hlsl/.bin sources. Source recovery/regeneration into an
   ignored analysis directory is prerequisite to claiming a proven rewrite;
   do not rebuild/replace the live cache without approval. Current translator
   source alone establishes late generic alpha-test emission, not a particular
   material's earliest safe discard point.
4. GPU resolve/presentation dataflow: do not repeat failed whole-target swap.
   Re-read current resolve path: every destination is kept in kept_resolves
   across frames, resolved_texture maps it for subsequent draws, final_texture
   simply tracks last colour resolve. Cropping/linear views, exponent bias,
   CPU writebacks, cube assembly and next-frame consumers complicate eliminating
   final/intermediate copies. Existing strict whole-target test had zero hits.
   A crop-aware/liveness-proven presentation bypass or cube-face path may
   save work, but a final-frame-only no-reader check does not prove next-frame
   safety. Keep as a second GPU route; no unsafe alias/direct-draw proposal.

### November 2: next target audit: sparse touch-overlay coverage (proposal only)

Stefan asks next optimization target after usable A/B analysis. Read-only audit
of current source and existing October18/19 attribute-key comparison tests,
October21 cost probe/October24 half-precision audit, November2 resolve-dataflow
negative record. Main fragment encoder remains~6.3ms, but dominance alone is
not a proven rewrite. Prior shader probe omits entire draws (includes raster/
vertex/overdraw), not an isolated fragment shader measurement. Cheap tree shader
has1fetch/3colour operations; gather/caster variants already exist. Repeating
broad fp16, early-alpha or already-implemented attribute/index cache changes is
not justified. Current resolve path retains destinations across frames, so
last-resolve/no-later-read within ONE frame is still not a safe copy-elimination
proof. No unsafe final-target alias or new scene rewrite proposed here.

Concrete different candidate found in native overlay path:
- ios/src/touch_controls.mm1510–1596: native touch view uses full-size screen-
  scale premultiplied BGRA backing image, clears/redraws only dirty rect with
  CGContext, passes complete backing pointer + dirty rect to renderer. View is
  nonopaque/clear. Existing changes already avoid unconditional full redraw.
- ios/src/native_renderer.mm8840ff: setter copies only dirty rows/columns into
  backing vector and unions dirty upload rectangle. Empty/resize behavior
  established here. Don't confuse changed rectangle with all visible pixels:
  unchanged controls outside it must continue to appear every rendered frame.
- mm7260–7310: renderer uploads changed rectangle, then EVERY frame with touch
  texture sets full-drawable viewport and full-drawable scissor and draws one
  fullscreen triangle. Thus transparent texture regions are still rasterized/
  sampled by this path even though they cannot change the output.
- OverlayPipeline4309–4340: same image sampled with linear/clamp_to_edge, no
  mips, output premultiplied; source RGB/alpha One, destination OneMinusSourceAlpha.
  Sampling all-zero BGRA is zero; blending is identity there. This is a concrete
  opportunity to avoid invoking fragments in provably zero regions, without
  moving controls, changing opacity, filter/UVs or game shaders. No claim Metal
  performs no internal transparent-blend optimizations; actual time benefit
  unknown. Existing final-pass code includes scene presentation and FPS overlay
  too, so final encoder median~0.65ms is NOT touch overlay cost or projected saving.

Proposed implementation only, NOT authorized by this question:
independent restart-only flag default FALSE; maintain coarse conservative
occupancy from all-channel-zero pixel checks on changed tiles only, including
cleared old locations. Pad occupied footprint for bilinear sampling and round
outwards in drawable mapping. Keep original full-screen viewport/UV mapping,
reuse original shader/pipeline/texture, restrict rasterization to a bounded set
of DISJOINT scissor rectangles; merge expanded halos so translucent pixels are
never blended twice. Dense/complex coverage uses legacy full-screen draw.
No scan of full image on every rendered frame. Coverage ownership/update under
existing mutex must match uploaded image; resize/disable/clear invalidates old
coverage. Preserve ordinary full-frame presentation and FPS rendering. Pure
native app draw/coverage change, no game metallib recompilation/recache intended.

Need before device: meaningful host coverage equivalence checks including
random dirty updates, clearing/moving/fading controls, all-zero/nonzero RGB with
alpha0, filter halos at screen edges and fractional scaling, disjointness and
resize/disable, full fallback. Track conservative submitted overlay pixels vs
full screen, number of extra draws and CPU coverage-update work so logical
reduction is distinguished from measured whole-frame GPU/energy saving.
One enabled visual/correctness device run if user approves; no new OFF baseline
requested now. Extra draw and CPU scan costs can offset GPU benefit; keep
bounded and optional until actual evidence. Expected scope modest; main-pass
material/overdraw investigation remains larger subsequent work.
