### 1. Confirmed omission: native guest face culling (recommended first trial)

Source observations:
- ios/src/native_renderer.mm1106 Draw stores depth/blend/color state, not guest
  cull/front-face mode. Record3063 reads PA_SU_SC_MODE_CNTL only for polygon
  offsets;3095 captures its window-offset enable. It never saves bits0–2.
- mm6447 explicitly relies on Metal culling default being OFF. No current
  setCullMode or setFrontFacingWinding call anywhere in native rendering path.
  Header comment28 lists culling among original missing features (other entries
  there are stale; omission confirmed by actual code, not comment alone).
- git log --all -S setCullMode finds d839985 and1b95c4e. Inspected both:
  original renderer explicitly set MTLCullModeNone; October12 commit1b95c4e
  merely removed that redundant call when adding state caching. It did NOT
  remove functioning guest culling after a failed test. No culling experiment
  found in targeted history/docs/HANDOFF searches. This is not a repeated trial.
- tools/ios/patch_ios_native_only.py98ff routes CP draws through the native hook
  before backend IssueDraw, bypassing SDK rasterizer/pipeline application while
  native-exclusive. Native CpDraw passes live register pointer into Record;
  register data is available at that moment, not retained by Draw afterward.
- Primary local SDK reference:
  `nfsmw-multiplayer-sdk/include/rex/graphics/registers.h`455ff: register0x2205,
  bit0cull_front,bit1cull_back,bit2face(0CCW/1CW).
  SDK graphics/d3d12/pipeline_cache.cpp1381ff and
  graphics/vulkan/pipeline_cache.cpp1632ff honor this for polygonal primitives.
  SDK graphics/util/draw.h61ff excludes points/lines/rectangle lists from this
  polygonal classification; draw.cpp66 handles both faces culled.
- Native index conversion2910ff turns rectangle lists into ordinary Metal
  triangles, just as fan/quad expansion does. Therefore final MTLPrimitiveType
  is INSUFFICIENT to decide whether guest culling applies: retain original
  primitive type. Do not accidentally cull HUD/post rectangle draws.

Potential: remove unwanted face rasterization/coverage/fragment work across
main, reflection, cube and shadow passes when the game requests culling. This
is true work removal, not only scheduling; broadly relevant to resolutions and
GPU families. Fixed-function face culling does NOT eliminate all vertex shader
work. Opaque back faces may already be rejected by depth/HSR, and some foliage
may intentionally be two-sided. Cannot claim half the draws/fragments/time,
current draw eligibility, or any battery saving. Existing snapshot/log omits
0x2205 bits0–2; affected counts and measured magnitude remain unknown.

Proposed ONLY, not implemented/approved:
`nfsmw_native_guest_culling=false` optional trial, capture guest cull/face/original
primitive state in Draw; decode exact none/front/back/both, preserve guest
intent including two-sided draws. Apply winding/cull state with encoder-reset
aware caching. Validate guest-to-Metal winding through actual native position/
viewport convention (native viewport takes abs scales; current scene sx>0/sy<0,
reflections/mirrors/internal/pixel-space shaders need specific checks). No blind
"cull back everywhere" switch. Unsupported primitive/coordinate cases retain
legacy path with counters. Both-face handling must preserve clears/resolves and
query semantics; query-sensitive and uncertain paths can initially fall back.
Host state/triangle-strip/fan/quad/rectangle/winding/reset checks before build.
Counters partition guest states, supported/fallback draws and submitted indices
by major target; these are NOT counts of rasterized or saved fragments.
Single enabled device correctness run on existing baseline settings after
approval, with ordinary menu/car/foliage/reflection/shadow observations. No new
shader compilation/rewrite expected from dynamic culling API state. No cache
clear or renewed D-017 experiment. Only useful measured GPU reduction merits
matched battery/thermal confirmation; larger effects remain unproven.

Apple primary reference: [setCullMode](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/mtlrendercommandencoder/setcullmode(_:))
and [front-facing winding](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/mtlrendercommandencoder/setfrontfacing(_:)):
culling is based on primitive orientation, with encoder default clockwise
front-facing orientation; correct guest mapping must be set explicitly.

### 2. Concrete broad scheduling lead: overdeclared texture reads

mm6208–6265 declares ALL current textures/resolved_textures/assembled_cubes/
volumes/cubes plus dummy_array/data as Read in BOTH Vertex and Fragment stages
on every render encoder. Dynamic buffer-backed crop and swizzle/cube views
mm6617/6635/6637/6690 also declare both stages. Conservative residency is
required; stage precision and actual pass consumers are not currently used.
Previous dev39–41 resource-list changes intentionally preserved this exact
GPU declaration: they saved CPU pointer construction, not these dependencies.

Read packaged dev41 IPA ZIP `Payload/NFSMW.app/NativeShaders/texture_masks.txt`:
42VS masks, ALL ZERO;59PS masks. Thus packaged translated VS interfaces do not
fetch textures according to existing metadata. Native internal VS interfaces
are registered with mask0 at mm804. Unknown shaders must retain conservative
fallback. Metadata ForDraw currently exposes only VS|PS union;
TextureMasks::Lookup is private and mutates recording-thread caches, so a render
thread must NOT start calling that cached lookup concurrently. Need immutable
stage-specific query or capture stage masks during Record.

Reanalyzed existing A/B compact exports only; script
`python3 ios/build/perf-gpu-nov2/structural-audit/analyze_overlap.py` exit0.
Same fully contained elapsed3–10s windows,419frames each; no fresh recording:

| metric, ms/frame mean | OFF run1 | ON run2 |
|---|---:|---:|
| active union, all app GPU stages |11.057798|11.169311|
| sum vertex active |1.121301|1.130155|
| vertex active without another app stage in same frame |1.094376|1.103222|
| vertex active without another app stage across ALL app frames |1.094053|1.103222|

~97.6% of vertex duration has no other app stage overlapping in these windows.
Second script pass checks non-vertex activity from ALL app frames, confirming
this is not primarily an artifact of excluding adjacent-frame overlap (exit0).
Example OFF traceframe479,elapsed5.007212291,9.815125ms envelope:
last cube blit17 completes1.592ms from frame start; main vertex18 starts1.592
and ends2.028; main fragment18 then2.028–7.428. This is serialization evidence,
NOT proof declared vertex texture reads caused it or all1.09ms is recoverable.
Real attachment hazards, shared target reuse and hardware scheduling also matter;
within-frame row excludes adjacent-frame overlap; all-app-frames row includes
it. Other processes are not represented by either metric.
Scheduling work more tightly is NOT eliminating1.09ms of shader execution or
proof of lower energy. No claim of a1ms saving yet.

Apple [useResources documentation](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/metal/mtlrendercommandencoder/useresources:count:usage:stages:)
confirms stages describe dependent shader stages and tracked declarations
participate in hazard handling. Local installed MTLRenderCommandEncoder.h966ff
also describes hazard protection and possible color attachment decompression;
current Read usage already minimizes one such risk. Apple's
[WWDC20 performance talk](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2020/10632/)
discusses false resource dependencies and stage overlap. Inference: declaring
texture reads for VS that never fetch may unnecessarily delay tiling; declaring
unrelated historical resolves may also add hazards/transitions. Must test cause,
not present source pattern as measured hardware causality.

Proposed architecture (secondary, unapproved): exact per-pass/per-stage consumer
sets, respecting resolve generations, aliases/cubes/views and all late-created
views; unknown metadata fallback BOTH/all as needed. Upload/constant/vertex data
remain declared in their actual required stages, shader argument heaps retained,
no residency calls simply deleted and no untracked hazards introduced. A narrower
first trial can change texture stages only on fully known no-texture VS passes,
with data buffer still both; exact pass filtering is further work. Keep isolated
from culling for attribution. CPU overhead of set planning also needs measuring.

### 3. Versioned render outputs: recurring copy traffic, not failed swap repeat

Parsed all snapshot resolves into ignored
`ios/build/perf-gpu-nov2/structural-audit/snapshot-resolves.json` (exit0):
18color+3depth. Important full-resolution events:
- resolve9: main depth after2487 ->08954000;
- resolve10: main color after2487 ->09689000, clearCD, exp0, swaptrue;
- resolve19: post color after2495 ->SAME09689000, no clear, exp0, swaptrue;
- resolve20: final color after2583 ->08dbb000, clearCD, exp0, swaptrue.
Scene and post physical targets2933x1320; sampled scene crop2859x1320,
guest rect1560x720 in pitch1568. Main target last draw2486; post target last2582.

Recovered baseline post shaders from existing local ISO with existing host tool,
only baseline rewrites, using ignored structural-audit/recover.py (exit0,
205valid containers,3matching/unique PS). No live shader/cache changes:
PS20710a9a2fef88e9 scene composite:12body tfetch2D sites including8DIFFUSEMAP
samples at different interpolated coordinates, other blur/depth/effect inputs.
PS36dac18d9d15b7a8: samples a distortion texture, transforms its values with
LocalCenter into coordinates for MISCMAP1, which current draw2495 binds to the
resolve19 image. Also samples opacity;20draws current post group. So post stage
really needs pre-overlay image at displaced coordinates while it draws back to
same target. Do not alias that resolve to writable target, fuse via simple
same-pixel framebuffer fetch, or call it a redundant copy. PS c39841aa2f3db228
blur has13body samples; not an identity copy. Generic post fusion is not proven.

More promising: source main color at resolve10 and completed post at resolve20
have no subsequent writes to their respective targets within this captured
frame. Versioned ownership can preserve these source generations rather than
copying into new textures. Existing target reuses texture next frame, while
kept_resolves promises old guest-address snapshots across frames, so generation
ownership must change. Safe retention must survive later clears, overwrites of
same guest resolve address, frames in flight, pool retirement and scale changes.
Source allocation dimensions differ from consumer dimensions: same-format view
of a private texture does not simply shrink it to the sampled crop. Need either
proven compact physical target bounds/consistent coordinate layout, or deferred
materialization/explicit coordinate handling. Compact target inference requires
ALL viewport/clip/pixel-space/resolve/consumer bounds, unavailable in current
partial snapshot; do not truncate just from these first group values.

Candidate two-copy payload:2*2859*1320*4=30191040bytes=28.792419MiB/frame,
1,811,462,400bytes/s at60 copies' one-direction logical payload; read+write
would be twice this UNCOMPRESSED arithmetic. This is not DRAM bandwidth,
compression/caches/energy or measured GPU saving. Does not include unavoidable
post resolve19 or depth copies. At other resolutions area changes, so structural
copy avoidance could scale with settings/devices, conditional on eligibility.

Final-output-only alternative: retain finished target generation for presentation
(crop already supported in presenter) and lazily materialize guest resolve only
if a future game consumer needs it. Requires versioning so a next-frame clear
cannot destroy retained image, and proper materialization before any shader sees
wrong dimensions. Presenter linear clamp is at physical texture edge, not crop
edge: add/prove correct half-texel crop clamping to avoid sampling padding when
upscaling. FXAA/MetalFX/motion/readback paths need fallback or separate proof.
No promise to eliminate presentation pass itself, which still fits/filter/blends
controls. Existing dev31 swap DID implement lifetime restores, but never applied
because full-target shape guard excluded all scene copies. Correcting earlier
commentary shorthand: it was shape eligibility, not an absence of any lifetime
handling in dev31. New work must solve cropped shapes, not rerun same switch.

### 4. Visibility/reordering conclusions and next decision

Current main1048groups all color maskF, with no grouped main-view depth-only
prepass. Recorded depth-only map563draws is light-space shadow generation,
NOT reusable camera depth. Thus earlier generic statement “existing depth-only
passes” does not mean current main already has a Z-prepass. Nonetheless a new
prepass is not automatically beneficial: Apple hardware removes hidden opaque
surfaces already, feedback/discard and blended fragments constrain it. Main
first cutout1440 precedes road1760; tree opaque1901/edge1902 then more opaque
cars2259. Ordering is unfavorable for maximum HSR but semantically constrained.
Moving all edge draws after later opaque surfaces can expose contributions that
were overwritten in original order; no image-equivalence proof. Preserve blend
order/depth ties/queries/resolves. Front-to-back sort or blind Z-prepass NOT
selected as a safe broad fix from these data.
Apple [HSR architecture talk](https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2020/10602/)
explains opaque/feedback/translucent grouping and blended visibility flushes;
WWDC20 performance talk above warns about unnecessary extra depth prepasses.
These support the constraints, not a quantified saving for this port.

Recommended order now: (1) isolated guest culling implementation/eligibility
trial, only after approval; (2) versioned cropped color/final-output ownership
for actual traffic removal; stage/pass resource precision is another independent
port-wide lead worth validating, not a guaranteed energy improvement. Priority
ranking is based on mechanism and evidence strength, not measured relative
savings (unknown). No additional user capture requested during this audit.

Implementation:
- `ios/src/native_guest_culling.h` pure production decision helper and cache.
  Guest bits0/1 select none/front/back/both; bit2 selects CCW/CW front orientation.
  Only original Xenos triangle list4/fan5/strip6/quad13 eligible; expanded
  rectangle8 and point/line types excluded. Original type/mode captured before
  the index-cache-hit branch, so cached Metal topology cannot change eligibility.

  special mirror viewport, incomplete X/Y viewport enable, nonfinite first4
  viewport floats, nonpositive sx or nonnegative sy. Existing native abs-scale
  viewport exactly matches guest window transform in supported sx>0/sy<0
  convention. Guest none preserves legacy None/CW without modifying shader
  front-facing classification; fallback also restores None/CW after eligible
  draws. Device winding/rendering validation still required; host algebra and
  primary SDK mapping aren't hardware image validation.

  cull/front-facing state only when enabled and state changes, no shader/PSO
  rewrite. EncoderState owns cache, reset by existing state.For path AND explicit
  state.enc=nil on new encoder (handles recycled object address/D-011).
- Eligible both-face draws don't issue raster draw or uploads after culling
  decision. Their recorded positions/targets/encoder clears and later resolves
  remain; query draws fall back. Existing sky-last stencil still only written by
  actual surviving draw fragments. No draw-order/attachment/residency changes.
- Per-target render-queue census for indexed draws reaching valid pipeline and

  both-face skips, fallback primitive/internal/query/viewport counts. Report/reset
  every300ordinary frames beside existing summaries, including OFF eligibility.
  Target-map lookup once per encoder; no per-draw map lookup. Snapshot frames
  excluded from census; snapshot diagnostic reports both-face skips separately.
  These are CPU-side submitted-input/state counts, NOT saved/rasterized faces,

## November 2, color-copy elimination design: compact scene image handoff proposed

Stefan says “let’s do it” after next priority was stated as render-target
copy-elimination DESIGN. Continued read-only investigation to form the concrete
implementation proposal required by his approve-before-source-change rule.
No renderer/header/test source edits, build, new IPA, default promotion or device
request in this turn. Start at85b6902, status only pre-existing HANDOFF_CHATGPT.md;
read AGENTS/checkpoint/backlog/latest evidence and git log15.

### Selected first mechanism: render into the shape the normal resolve already uses

Initial thought was finished-frame resolve20. Further code audit finds MAIN
resolve10 a better first implementation: its normal destination already becomes
a private/tiled single-size texture under existing nfsmw_native_tiled_crops.
Current main source is2933x1320, while sampled resolve shape is2859x1320
(guest1560x720 at scale1.833). Plan the eligible source's physical color/depth
attachment width to that same sampled shape, preserve the native viewport and
all shader inputs, then hand the completed COLOR IMAGE to the resolve instead
of copying it. Target receives a different reusable image for its next clear.
No per-fetch UV remap, altered game shader or final presentation crop needed.
When source already has that exact destination shape (possible other settings/
devices), no compaction needed, but versioned ownership still required.

This is an architectural change, not a retry of dev31's unchanged full-size
swap. Dev31 could not apply because source/destination shapes differed and had
load restores. This design explicitly reconciles physical source shape with the
EXISTING normal private resolve shape and requires an after-last-draw/clear
boundary, avoiding a later load/restore of donated image. Only one source color
resolve allowed in initial plan. Main/source scene candidate has1048draws,
resolve9depth then10color at2487, color clearCD; no subsequent draw on source.
One observed frame suggests candidate, not proof every runtime frame eligible:
dump lacks all consumer descriptors and feature would be disabled during dump.
Runtime planner must check ALL actual consumers, not assume one sampled size.

Relevant source findings in current ios/src/native_renderer.mm:
- Px461 rounds double(guest)*float(scale) with lround. Target sizing5067 uses
  EDRAM pitch; normal resolve-layout logic5655ff independently fits sampled
  one-size cropped image. Share that layout decision between planner/resolve,
  rather than maintaining two drifting approximations.
- SourceTarget.t.pitch/t.height are physical dimensions, distinct from raw
  EDRAM layout key and sizes map. Keep raw guest pitches for keys/small-target
  policy, change only approved physical allocation width. Recompute same plan
  each frame so target-size cache doesn't alternate padded/compact allocations.
- Normal translated viewport setup6480ff depends on guest viewport and t.scale,
  not attachment width. Width/height-sensitive handwritten/pixel-space/mirror/
  motion paths are specifically excluded. Scissor is whole target, so geometry
  sample coverage must be proved before shrinking attachment, not inferred only
  from final rectangle.
- Normal do_resolve registers GPU heap slot, resolved_texture/swap/scale,
  kept_resolves, final-image selection, resolve count and clear flags. Handoff
  must preserve these operations and only remove allocation/copy of destination.
  Keep existing source store action (image will be sampled). Depth conversion,
  bloom, intermediate distortion copy and presenter all stay as before.
- A subtle same-address generation: MAIN resolve10 and later POST resolve19 both
  write09689000. Post resolve19 must retire the old main image only after FRAME
  completion; earlier draws already encoded still reference it. Existing
  resolved_views keys use physical texture identity and each resolve appends a
  new heap slot, so old slot/view identity can be preserved without changing
  shader binding semantics. Don't overwrite old heap entries in place.
- Original GpuPool only owns resolve/buffer allocations. Target color is currently
  standalone; adding an image to its raw pointer-key table does NOT itself retain
  it. Adopt a donated target into pool ownership without duplicating existing
  residency Add, keep strong resolve/retirement references, and lease replacement
  using RT|ShaderRead descriptor. Set BOTH src.color and src.multisample_color
  (1x) to replacement. Depth object unchanged except approved width allocation.
- Existing target-size/sample-count replacement5074ff unconditionally removes
  color residency. For pool-owned target colors, instead retire exactly once
  after current frame fence; never Remove/free while pool or GPU still owns it.
  Persist pooled-ownership bit across normal per-frame resets; clear only on
  genuine ownership replacement. Pool must never return current target/kept/
  retired-but-not-completed images for reuse. Old standalone color adopts once.
  Target changes scale/sample count, frame snapshots and scene transitions must
  exercise both cleanup paths. FrameDoneOnGpu is completion-prefix authority on
  the single queue; don't reclaim merely when CPU encoding returns.

### Proposed eligibility and fail-closed behavior

Proposed flag `nfsmw_native_color_handoff=false`, restart-only, still NOT added.
OFF bypasses planner/allocation/ownership changes. ON initial trial:
1. Ordinary displayed frame, lazy diagnostics; no dump/GPU capture, temporal
   MetalFX/motion-debug or cost probe/split experiment. Existing culling setting
   stays separately controlled, default false unchanged.
2. Color scene-sized target (guest pitch640+), RGBA8Unorm, one sample, no MRT.
   Exactly one ordinary color resolve from this source, at last source draw's
   boundary, clear-color set, top-left full sampled rectangle, exp_bias0, supported
   destination format/endian, no array/cube assembly destination or CPU writeback.
   Reject ambiguous source-layout fallback; don't infer final-only from ordinal.
3. Run canonical existing resolve-layout decision on ORIGINAL dimensions and
   all Frame::textures consumer descriptors. Require private/non-buffer/tiled
   output, one physical size, rectangle fills that complete output, same format,
   same source height (width-only compaction initially), dimensions<=8192. Don't
   shrink to a convenient guessed width or treat a linear/buffer view as a crop
   of a private texture. Every source depth/other read rect must still fit.
4. Analyze ALL source draws: clipped triangle rasterization, full ordinary X/Y
   viewport enables, finite scale/offset, sx>0/sy<0, no internal/pixel-space/
   special mirror path, no query or MRT. No later source writes or mid-generation
   color snapshot. All visible sample centers inside compact physical extent;
   bound actual native float viewport calculations, not rough integer viewport.
   For 1x sampling require left/top>=0 and right<width+0.5,bottom<height+0.5,
   so sample centers beyond compact edge could not have been covered before.
   Native XY clip/viewport and pixel grid stay identical for surviving area;
   exclude uncertain edge/coordinate cases rather than silently cropping them.
5. Before donating, revalidate actual descriptor/source/resolve layout and lease
   compatible replacement. If replacement unavailable/budget exceeded, perform
   normal copy, keep original target owner. A validated compact target still
   produces same normal resolve in this fallback. Bound version leases (proposed
   max4images/descriptor plus128MiB total lease budget; fallback when busy/too
   large), report actual allocated bytes/high water. Those are proposed limits,
   not measured memory gains. At high scales budget may intentionally retain
   copy path. No fresh allocations every frame once compatible leases reusable.
6. On success register finished old color as resolve with existing metadata,
   retire any overwritten kept image through existing frame fence, rotate target
   color to replacement, preserve resolves_done/clear logic. No restore blit:
   source has no subsequent writes this frame and next frame starts cleared.
   Don't place persistent replacement in FrameResources automatic retirement.

Gather analysis using existing target-sizing traversal and per-target summaries
where practical, avoiding new per-draw map lookups or geometry transforms. Do
not spend more CPU on planning than the removed work warrants. Counters when ON:
eligible/planned targets, handoffs, fallback reasons/allocation misses, explicit
copies remaining, eliminated logical payload bytes, image leases/reuses/retirements
and actual memory bounds. Counts define removed commands/payload, NOT physical
DRAM traffic, power, saved shading or FPS. Preserve other pool/residency flags.

### Why final output and post fusion are deferred

Final resolve20 has no current-frame shader consumer known in snapshot, so its
normal destination may be linear pitch1568, not sampled-size tiled1560. Source
handoff there would require lazy future materialization/shape metadata or a more
substantial target-layout redesign to preserve later game reads. Existing
presenter clamps at physical texture edge, not crop edge, so direct padded source
sampling also needs careful half-texel treatment. This trial leaves that whole
path unchanged. Post resolve19 is needed by displacement sampling in PS36dac18d;
no simple same-pixel framebuffer-fetch merge. No generic full-frame post rewrite.

### Existing trace bounds: real transfer work, modest frame-time opportunity

Reanalyzed existing dev41 A/B compact exports, same fully-contained3–10s elapsed
windows/419frames per arm, no new recording/export. Command mapping follows
source+snapshot structure; generic encoder ordinals are scoped to these traces.
`python3 ios/build/perf-gpu-nov2/color-handoff-design/trace_copy_spans.py` exit0:

| encoder | OFF mean span ms/frame | ON mean | OFF time without other app-stage overlap | ON equivalent |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Blit20, main color copy |0.351176|0.353632|0.156883|0.156977|
| Blit36, pre-distortion post copy |0.158886|0.159736|0.158886|0.159736|
| Blit38, final picture copy |0.197219|0.202801|0.197219|0.202801|

Main copy overlaps depth conversion. Removing its command is NOT a promise of
0.35ms shorter frame; exclusive interval also isn't a predictive critical-path
simulation. Real scheduling/cache/compression changes require device evidence.
This is not a halving-of-GPU-time proposal; dominant main shading still remains.
Payload for one eligible native main image2859*1320*4=15095520bytes,
14.396210MiB/frame. Uncompressed read+write arithmetic at60 is1,811,462,400
bytes/s; at1x or other devices scales with actual image area. Not measured DRAM,
compression-adjusted bandwidth, energy or thermal saving. Do NOT reuse earlier
28.792MiB TWO-copy figure for this first single-copy trial.

## November 2, dev43 color handoff implementation: host/build checked, device pending

Stefan approved implementing only the isolated default-OFF trial from “color-copy
elimination design” above. Nothing else changed: culling default stays false,
final-output/post/dependency work stays deferred, no default promotion.

Implementation (`ios/src/native_renderer.mm`):
- `nfsmw_native_color_handoff=false`, restart-only (read once). OFF: no plan,
  no pooled target colors, no handoff; every new branch is gated by it.
- Frame-level exclusion when ON: dump, non-lazy diagnostics, GPU capture,
  MetalFX temporal, motion debug, cost probe, pass split, tiled crops off.
- `resolve_layout` lambda: the existing do_resolve rectangle/destination and
  tiled-crop decision moved verbatim into one helper used by BOTH do_resolve and
  the planner (no second approximation). Fit loop now also skipped for cube
  (array) resolves, which never used it.
- Setup loop (ON only): per target, reject on any draw that is not a full-VTE
  (x/y scale+offset) translated viewport with sx>0, sy<0, finite offset, original
  primitive 4/5/6/8/13, no query, no MRT, not mirror PS, not internal VS; keeps
  last draw index and up to 16 distinct (x scale, x offset) pairs.
- Planner per scene target (pitch640+, not shadow): RGBA8, 1 sample, not a
  second target; exactly one color resolve sourced from it (source chosen as
  do_resolve chooses), rt0, clear-color, exp_bias0, not array, no write-back,
  after its last draw. Normal layout on ORIGINAL size must be tiled, top-left,
  fill fit_w x fit_h, fit_h == target height, fit_w <= pitch. Every resolve
  from the target (depth too) must have Px(x1) <= fit_w; every viewport right
  edge, computed in the draw loop's float then double, < fit_w + 0.5. Planned:
  target physical width = fit_w (height, viewport, scissor rule, shaders
  unchanged). Census per plan outcome.
- Planned targets take their color from GpuPool (RT|ShaderRead|resolve view
  usage, private). A target already of the planned size but standalone is
  adopted once (new `GpuPool::Adopt`, no second residency Add) instead of being
  remade; pool-owned colors are Retired after the frame on resize, never
  residency-Removed while in use. `GpuPool::live` counts objects per kind;
  `Texture(..., most)` returns nil rather than make one past `most`.
- do_resolve: on the planned resolve, revalidates pooled, 1 sample, color
  attachment == color, top-left full fit rect, exact image size/format and
  usage, exp_bias0; then leases a same-descriptor replacement (at most
  min(4, 128MiB/image) of that kind). Success: dest = finished image, target
  color/multisample_color = replacement, no blit encoded; heap slot, resolved
  maps, kept_resolves retirement, cube assembly, final selection, clear flags
  and write-back path all unchanged. Lease miss/mismatch: normal tiled copy.
- Pass begin counts passes on a target after its handoff (plan excludes them;
  must stay 0). Summary every 300 frames when ON only: plans
  planned/draws/viewports/target/resolves/layout/extent, frames excluded,
  copies not encoded + logical MiB, pool misses, mismatches, late passes, most
  images of the kind. Counts are commands/payload, NOT DRAM traffic or energy.
- Known limit (inference): a later frame resolving this target WITHOUT drawing
  it would read the uncleared replacement instead of the stale image; the
  planned resolve clears color, so neither was faithful. Not seen in snapshot.

## November 3, iPad crash loop: pipeline cache save aborts in Metal; dev46 self-heal

Report: iPad16,6, iPadOS 27.2 (24B119), LiveContainer 3.8.11, app UUID
c2bb4003-cc69-38db-94b7-2deeded2073b, native 2.867. Crashes ~15 s after every

and `ipad_pipeline_cache_crash_nfsmw.log` (four launches appended, each ends
the same way; the first "game: starting" line only once).
Crash (measured): EXC_CRASH SIGABRT, thread `MTLBinaryArchive`: std::terminate
from `std::__throw_out_of_range` in Metal, under `-[_MTLBinaryArchive
loadAirntBlocksForSlice:...]` ← `loadFromURL:` ← `airntSerializeToURL:` —
i.e. our background `serializeToURL:` in `PipelineArchive::Report`. Log: cache
loaded (68295 KiB), ps_684f alpha variants missed and added, crash ~2 s after
the next 300-frame summary (01:28:04 → capture 01:28:06), the save point.

serializing re-reads every entry and Metal throws an uncatchable C++ exception.

and crashes; builds that added nothing never saved. Cause of the damage unknown.

`serializeToURL:` and removed after it returns; `Open` finding the marker deletes
the archive and starts a new one (warning logged). At most one more crash, then
one launch of recompiling (stutter). No switch; affects all devices/players.

### November 3: why the earlier judder fixes do not cover the iPad camera sawtooth

Stefan asks how to fix the iPad (Codex's earlier world/camera timing changes
fixed the general judder). Comparing the 1.5x iPad Max log with the iPhone log:
- World step identical on both: fixed given 16.667 ms (mode 2), output
  pattern 16.667/16.667/16.389 ms (60/60/59 ticks) every 3 frames — iPad 2774
  60-tick / 1376 59-tick, iPhone 2863 / 1391. Sim rate 120 on both.
- Host gaps are NOT the difference: iPad sd 2.72 ms, iPhone sd 3.19 (more
  uneven) yet the iPhone camera is smooth.
- iPad camera sawtooth values are close to 1:2:3 (0.32 / 0.64 / 0.95), as if
  the camera advanced by a varying number of 120 Hz substeps per frame on the
  iPad only. Not verified: no per-frame substep count is logged.
Conclusion: the existing fixes work on the iPad too; the remaining cause is
iPad-specific and unidentified. Proposed (needs approval): a diagnostic-only
log of 120 Hz substeps per displayed frame and of the camera update count, to
see where the iPad diverges, before any fix. Candidate fix to test afterwards:
remove the 59-tick output frame so every frame gets exactly 2 substeps.

Follow-up (Stefan approved the substep/camera logging build): read
`ios/generated/default/nfsmw_recomp.108.cpp` sub_823C6500 (where
nfsmw_world_step_trace sits). It converts accumulated time to integer world
ticks (r30, 3600/s: 60 or 59 per frame), stores them (0x82A2CD14) and the
float step; it has no 120 Hz substep loop. The substeps happen further
downstream (not yet located), so a true per-frame substep counter needs that
code found first. Arithmetic check: with 30 ticks per 120 Hz step, the
60/60/59 pattern yields a 1-step frame only about once per 30 cycles, not a
persistent 3-frame sawtooth, and the same pattern is on the iPhone. So the
1:2:3 hypothesis is weakened (inference). Cheaper discriminator proposed
before more reverse engineering: iPad, same lap/args, plus
`--nfsmw_sim_rate=60`; if the camera pattern changes, the cause is tied to the
120 Hz simulation and the hook point is in that path. No code changed.

iPad sim-rate 60 result (dev47, Max, 1.5x, same lap/args + `--nfsmw_sim_rate=60`;
`dev47_ipad_sim60_camera_nfsmw.log`). Stefan: "pretty sure it felt better now";
also: the full-screen Extra arguments editor works well ("fire").
Camera zigzag (same metric): 48 of 1632 moving frames (2.9%), vs 37.6% at
sim 120 on the same iPad; only 2 still frames between moving ones (no return of
the Oct 29 start-of-pursuit 2-of-3 freeze). Pacing 0–46 of 300 off grid, last
windows 0–2. Conclusion: the iPad camera sawtooth is caused by the 120 Hz
simulation on the iPad (sim 120 is what fixed the iPhone). Mechanism inside
the game's 120 Hz path still unknown. Proposed (needs approval): launcher
passes sim 60 below the 120 cap on 6+ efficiency-core devices (tablet profile),
120 elsewhere and at the 120 cap (which needs it).

### November 3: iPad 120 Hz sawtooth lead — world quantum sits exactly on the 2-substep boundary

Stefan rejects per-device sim 60 (120 fps on the iPad needs sim 120): fix the
120 Hz simulation itself. Only measured difference found between the devices
in the world clock: the display period used as the world quantum.
`[world-clock]` quantum: iPad 16.6667 ms (exact 60 Hz from ProMotion), iPhone
16.6682 ms (+1.5 µs). Two 1/120 s steps are exactly 16.6667 ms, so on the iPad
each frame's time lands on the boundary of the guest's 120 Hz step
accumulator, where float rounding can give 1, 2 or 3 steps (fits the ~1:2:3
camera ratios); the iPhone's 1.5 µs surplus keeps it at 2 (a 3rd step only
every few thousand frames). Inference, not verified in guest code (substep
loop not located; many readers of the 1/120 constant).
Proposed experiment (needs approval): cvar `nfsmw_world_quantum_bias_us`
(default 0) adding a few µs to the world quantum in AdvanceWorldClock's
period; test 2 on the iPad at sim 120. Long-term world speed changes by
~0.01%; existing debt resync bounds the drift.

## November 3, 120 Hz step loop found: steps counted at 60/s, subtracted at 1/120; dev49 experiment

Stefan approved step 1 (fix the 120 Hz step loop properly). Found in generated
USA code (`ios/generated/default`): sub_823C66C8 (nfsmw_recomp.91.cpp) and
sub_823C6858 (nfsmw_recomp.23.cpp) add the frame time (0x82A39660, written by
sub_823C6500 as world ticks × step) to an accumulator (0x82A2CD18 /
0x82A2CD1C area), take steps = fctiwz(acc × [0x82057114]) with a minimum of 1,
and subtract steps × [0x820AFDD0]. Inspection image
(`ios/build/managed40-inspection-image.bin`, original values): 0x82057114 =
60.0, 0x820AFDD0 = 1/60. Our sim-rate patch changes only 0x820AFDD0 (and
0x828F85AC) to 1/120, so at 120 Hz the loops count with the 60 Hz rule and
subtract 1/120 per step: steady state keeps ~16.7–33.3 ms in the accumulator
(two steps' worth) instead of < one step. Also read: sub_824CF3A8 integrates
in ≤1/120 s slices to a continuous target time (not quantized; not the cause);
World_Service sub_824CE048 only stores its timestep.
Offline float32 model (input pattern 60/60/59 ticks per frame, or constant)
gives the same step counts with the original, plain-120 and fixed rules (2 per
frame, rare 1s), so it does NOT reproduce the iPad sawtooth; the measured
quantum-bias effect therefore acts somewhere this model omits. The counting
inconsistency is real, its effect on the camera unproven.
Change: `tools/ios/patch_game_sim_steps.py` (new, apply/--status/--revert,
idempotent; added to generate_code.py after world_step_trace; applied to the
local generated code) routes the 60.0 load in both functions through
`nfsmw_sim_steps_per_second` (game_extra_options.cpp). New cvar
`nfsmw_sim_step_count` (default false): at sim 120 returns 120 × (1+1e-4)
(tolerance so an exact two-step frame is not truncated to one), else the
game's value; logs `[extra-options] sim step count: ...` once.
Checks: patch script status/apply twice (idempotent), patch_game_extra_options
exit0, build-0.6 ipa exit0, `git diff --check` exit0, binary contains the log
string; ZIP vs dev48 only the executable changed. IPA
`ios/build/NFSMW-0.6.0-dev49-sim-step-count.ipa` (and Desktop), 30580703
bytes, SHA256 af03a4e36b01755e48e90581512388910be65a36262fd5fe968160b1221b9469.
Test: iPad Max 1.5x sim 120, four diagnostic args, NO quantum bias, plus
`--nfsmw_sim_step_count=true`; compare zigzag with 37.6% (none) / 5.7% (bias).

dev49 iPad result (`dev49_ipad_sim_step_count_nfsmw.log`, Max, 1.5x, sim 120,
step count on, bias 0; Stefan: "still felt off, at least at the start").

The iPhone without bias runs ~0.009% fast vs a nominal 60 Hz because its
measured period is 16.6682 ms (if the panel is truly nominal). Option offered:
pay the bias back periodically to make long-term drift zero.

New cvar `nfsmw_native_record_memo` (false, restart-only):
- Index fingerprint memo: IndexEntry gains `verified_frame`/`changed_frame`.
  A cached index buffer already verified this frame and unchanged for > 2
  frames skips IndexFingerprint (same rule as the vertex memo: a stable
  buffer rewritten mid-frame is noticed next frame; recently changed buffers
  are hashed every draw).
- Per-entry vertex memo: CacheEntry keeps the region (base/start/size) and
  fingerprint taken this frame; a repeat skips the frame-wide memo's
  unordered_map lookup (same eligibility: not dynamic, not UP vertices).
- Constant ranges: last vs/ps key per stage reuses the found range across a
  run of draws (fallback range {0,256} is conservative).
- Summary line `[native] record memo on ...: N index fingerprints and M vertex
  memo lookups skipped`. OFF leaves every path unchanged.

## November 4: dev55 exact-wake frame hand-off waits (on by default)

Stefan chose the proper fix over a fixed sleep length (a fixed length may not
suit slower devices). Generated code (USA, ios/generated/default): the hand-off
word 0x82A2CF40 (base 0x82A30000 = lis -32093, offset -12480) has exactly two
stores in the generated code (all six `+ -12480` references checked: 2 in
sub_82441B60 loads + 1 store, 2 loads in sub_82441DB0, 1 store in
sub_82441EF0): sub_82441EF0 stores 1 (main loop hands a frame over),
sub_82441B60 stores 0 (r26 = 0, render thread done). Waits: sub_82441B60 loops
on Sleep(0) (sub_8262D790, lr 0x82441BBC) while the word is 0; sub_82441DB0
loops (lr 0x82441E4C) while it is 1. So the ~6,900 wakes/s of Nov 4 are the
two sides of one handshake.

Change: `tools/ios/patch_game_handoff_wait.py` (4 sites, apply/--status/
--revert; also run by generate_code.py after sim_steps) replaces those two
Sleep(0) calls with `if (!nfsmw_handoff_wait(base, value)) sub_8262D790(...)`
and adds `nfsmw_handoff_wake(base)` after both stores. New
`ios/src/game_handoff_wait.cpp` (in CMake's game sources):
os_sync_wait_on_address_with_timeout on the guest word (big-endian raw
compare), os_sync_wake_by_address_all after each store; cvars
`nfsmw_handoff_wait` (true, restart-only; false = the game's Sleep(0)
polling, i.e. dev54 behaviour) and `nfsmw_handoff_wait_us` (2000, safety-net
timeout 100–50000); log `[handoff-wait] on ...` once and `[handoff-wait] 10 s:
N waits (R/s), T timed out, K wakes sent`. dev54's `ios_delay0_us` stays
(default 100); its `[delay0]` rate now shows the remaining zero-length polls.
Checks: patch apply/revert/apply round trip OK, status 4/4; host model
(scratchpad handoff_test.cpp, same wait/wake on a byteswapped word, two
threads, clang++ -O2): 200000 hand-offs in 0.58 s (2.9 us each), 389413
waits, 0 timeouts, exit 0 (model, not the game). `patch_game_extra_options.py`

pre-existing SDK fpscr.h warning); `unzip -t` OK; codesign deep/strict exit0;

## November 4: why the frame submit is expensive (Mac micro-benchmark, code reading)

Stefan approved the submit/Record investigation (iPhone E-core question moved to
a separate thread). Code: one frame command buffer per frame (`[queue
commandBuffer]`, retained references; early commit off), plus the BC-decode
queue's buffers; a queue residency set (`residency::Apply`, initialCapacity
4096) holds arena chunks, pool buffers and textures; geometry is sub-allocated
from the geometry arena (GpuBufferFor -> buffer_arena chunks), so vertex and
index buffers are few allocations; textures and render targets are one
allocation each (272 textures in use per frame in the Time Profile run's log,
21 resolves); per-encoder useResources declares ~259 entries per summary.
Host micro-benchmark (scratchpad submit_bench.mm, M2 Pro Mac, Metal, 300
frames each, one compute encoder per command buffer, process CPU via
getrusage): residency-set size does not matter (0/1k/4k/16k allocations:
0.02–0.04 ms/frame empty); distinct buffers bound per command buffer do:
300 distinct 0.12–0.19 ms CPU (0.05–0.10 ms kernel), 2000 distinct 0.51–0.63
ms (0.16–0.23 ms kernel); the same 2000 binds over 8 distinct buffers 0.25 ms
(0.04 ms kernel); unretained command buffers ~20 % less CPU at equal binds.
Inference: the iPad's ~0.8 ms kernel time per frame submit scales with the
number of distinct allocations (textures, render targets, pool buffers) the
frame's command buffer references, on a slower E core; sub-allocating static
game textures from MTLHeaps (useHeap, few allocations) and unretained command
buffers would cut it. Both are lifetime/hazard-sensitive changes (heap
textures are untracked; BC-decoded textures come from another queue).
Expected energy effect small on E cores (render queue already Utility);
not started. Waiting for Stefan's floor (home screen) and scale 1.0 runs to
size what is reachable toward 20 %/h.

Options discussed with Stefan: A (half the cube faces) = existing "Car
reflections: Half each frame"; dropped. Fixed reflection rates: BACKLOG,

receivers, so removal needs shader changes; parked in BACKLOG. B split into

image, ~0.2 ms, needs bounds for its non-viewport-transformed draws, guard 0
"vte", ps 8c8b535864c59f03).

B1 built as dev76: `nfsmw_native_sparse_touch_overlay` (default false,
restart-only). The setter keeps a 32x32 tile occupancy grid of the touch
picture (a tile counts if any non-zero pixel lies within 2 px of it, the
bilinear reach), rescanned only for tiles touching the dirty rectangle. On
upload the renderer turns occupied tiles into disjoint rectangles (row runs
merged downward when spanning the same columns; >64 falls back to the full
draw) and draws the same overlay triangle once per rectangle with a scissor;
tile edges are mapped to drawable pixels with one shared rounding so
rectangles never overlap (no double blending). Every 1800 frames it logs
draws per frame and the share of the screen blended. Off: unchanged code
path. Not host-tested; build `cmake --build ~/Library/Caches/nfsmw-ios/build-0.6
--target ipa -j 12` exit 0 (19 s incremental), `unzip -t` OK, `git diff
--check` clean. IPA `ios/build/NFSMW-0.6.0-dev76-sparse-touch-overlay.ipa`,

### November 5: dev77 cost probe, iPhone native 60: trees dominate

Log `Debug/5 November 2026/dev77_iphone_native60_cost_probe_nfsmw.log`
(SHA256 475cb572…), iPhone, dev77, native/60 Balanced,
`--nfsmw_native_cost_probe=true --nfsmw_native_pass_counters=true`. Median
GPU time saved when a pixel shader's draws are left out (vs the 8 frames
before; includes vertex/raster/overdraw; single-sample outliers ignored):

| ps | samples | median saved ms | draws/frame |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 27d82ea0faa380a8 (trees) | 14 | 2.74 (0.88-4.77) | 477 |
| fe510d2d256c173b (sky) | 10 | 1.02 | 8 |
| 4fbaecfb8e7c4f40 (shadow casters) | 5 | 0.78 | 456 |
| d1a189fdbb29cf1a | 8 | 0.69 | 40 |
| 684f4711f29b9f77 (fences/plants) | 9 | 0.46 | 542 |
| d8bb87fee2d8ec76 | 9 | 0.36 | 126 |
| others | | < 0.35 | |

Trees (cost-state lines) are drawn twice in every target (main d468, cube
d7c0, mirror d71a): an opaque core pass (alpha test GEQUAL 0.706 or 0.392,
no blend, depth 0x736 = test LEQUAL + write) and a matching edge pass
(alpha test LESS, same ref, blend 0x07060706 src-alpha, depth 0x732 = test
LEQUAL, no write), with equal draw counts. In the edge pass every pixel
the core pass wrote passes the LEQUAL depth test (same depth) and then runs
the full shader only to be discarded by the alpha test. Lead (proposal, not
built): for ps 27d82ea0 edge-pass draws use LESS instead of LEQUAL, so those
pixels are rejected by the depth test before shading. Same picture except
exact depth ties with other geometry; saving unknown (part of 2.74 ms).

Sky-wait census: in the cube faces and mirror the sky's wait always ends at
once (0 solid draws before it), at ps 684f / f1f0e5ca with colour mask 7:
`opaque()` required mask 0xF, and those targets write RGB only (sky too).

ps 20710a9a (recovered baseline in ignored `ios/build/perf-gpu-nov2/structural-audit/`):
colour = sharp + amount * (7 offset scene taps combined - sharp), with
amount = saturate((blurmap.x + BlurParams.x) * saturate(-rcp(1 - depth) *
c254.x + c255.y) + BlurParams.y * blurmap.w). Where amount is exactly 0 the
taps (finite samples) contribute nothing.

dev80 adds two default-off restart-only trials:
- `nfsmw_native_post_blur_skip`: new `tools/native/rewrite_post_blur_skip.py`
  (run by build_shaders.sh after the foliage rewrite; body-digest guarded)
  gives ps 20710a9a a specialization bit 14 (0x4000) that computes the
  amount first with the same operations in the same order and fetches the 7
  offset taps only where it is not 0 (NaN keeps them); unset = original.
  Renderer sets the bit for that shader's draws; a failed variant returns
  nil (like bit 13); counted in the early-commit summary line. Library
  rebuilt alone from the recovered baseline hlsl with the build_shaders
  commands (iOS 18.0); the baseline recompiled here has the same size as the
  cached library but 92 differing bytes (two 32-byte hash blocks, a 16-byte
  id and 12 single bytes), so the bit-off path is a recompile of the same
  translation, not byte-identical. Previous library kept at
  `~/Library/Caches/nfsmw-ios/shaders/previous/ps_20710a9a2fef88e9.metallib.pre-dev80`;
  new SHA256 ab7ca29a…eca1c. No host GPU equivalence test (inputs are
  bindless heaps); the taps sit in non-uniform control flow, exact for the
  single-level resolve texture. First launch recompiles that pipeline.
- `nfsmw_native_sky_last_masked`: sky-last also accepts solid draws whose
  colour mask is non-zero and covers every channel the sky writes.

### November 6: dev83 result (copies never read); dev84 skips unread large resolves (default off)

Log `Debug/6 November 2026/dev83_iphone_native60_linear_resolve_watch_nfsmw.log`
(SHA256 4379695a…), Stefan drove and opened the pause menu (fine). Both
watched destinations: "not sampled in 1200 frames (601 writes)" for
08dbb000 (1560x720) and 09222000 (2859x1320), in both sessions of the log.
The renderer binds a resolve only to textures naming its address, so a copy
no texture names cannot reach the picture. Inference: the game's own
consumer of these (if any) is not reached in normal driving.
dev84: `nfsmw_native_skip_unread_resolves` (default false, restart-only).
Each frame adds every texture address to `ever_sampled`; a colour, non-cube
resolve of >= 1M pixels to an address never named since launch is skipped
(its clears still applied), except the frame's last colour resolve (the
displayed one) and a planned colour-handoff resolve. Logs the first skip
per destination, "sampled now ... copied again" if one is named later (that
first frame would read guest memory instead: one-frame risk), and the skip
count in the early-commit summary line. Build exit 0, `unzip -t` OK. IPA
`ios/build/NFSMW-0.6.0-dev84-skip-unread-resolves.ipa` (SHA256 a472b44271ea82f32e15ed5f427417329fbf8ddc70fbf9202140061e2c96f85e), on the
